This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a verbal n-back working memory task (an established executive function). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. The authors report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (one-sample and two-sample t tests) and provide coordinates, cluster-level thresholds, tables and figures for within-group contrasts (n-back [1-2-3] vs 0-back) for each participant group. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (task domain = working memory; fMRI; whole-brain voxelwise group analyses; within-group task contrasts) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, empirical human imaging data). Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical fMRI task-based investigation using the Stroop task (inhibition/selective attention), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level statistical parametric maps (SPM99) and provides within-group task contrasts for both TBI patients and healthy controls (group activation maps, tables and figures). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (group pooled maps), and results are reported in tables/figures. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (operation span), an executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with corrected thresholds and tables/coordinates, within-group task contrasts (Arithmetic+Memory vs single-task and task vs baseline), and reports results in figures/tables. Participants are healthy adults and a within-group contrast is provided. All inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (a core executive function) using a stop-signal paradigm. It reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (successful vs failed stop trials; one-sample t test across 24 subjects and group-wise median-split contrasts), with tables/figures of coordinates and statistical maps. Participants are healthy adults. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function (set-shifting) using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task, which falls squarely within cognitive flexibility. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with appropriate multiple-comparison correction and cluster thresholds, and presents within-group task contrasts for both the Parkinson’s and matched control groups (e.g., receiving negative feedback minus control feedback, matching after negative feedback minus control matching). Results are reported in tables and text (peak coordinates, cluster sizes). Participant groups include clinical (PD) and healthy controls. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a stop-signal task (inhibition) — an established executive function domain. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, random-effects group contrasts (e.g., stop success > stop error; stop > go) with whole-brain analyses and coordinate tables/figures. Thus it meets I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (inhibition), I7 (group-level voxelwise/whole-brain results), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/figures). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; not truncated. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an event-related fMRI study of cognitive set shifting (WCST) in healthy adults, reporting group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses with coordinates and figures. It assesses cognitive flexibility (executive function), includes within-group contrasts (1st-round vs 2nd-round shifts and shifts vs correct trials), and provides whole-brain voxelwise results (with some SVC for DLPFC but not limited to ROI-only reporting). Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI studies and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study tests working memory/binding tasks (meets I5, I6), reports within-group task contrasts (I8), includes an eligible participant group (I9), and reports results in text/figures/coordinates (I10). However, the authors explicitly state they ‘used the clusters of activation found in that study as a mask, applying those regions of interest…’ and computed ROI-based percentage signal change for planned comparisons rather than reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps. Thus it does not provide voxelwise whole-brain activation results and qualifies as an ROI-only analysis, meeting exclusion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task maps). Exclusion criteria applied: E3. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (two-back), an established executive function domain. Methods describe whole-brain EPI acquisition and voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM99 analyses; results include within-group task contrasts for patients and controls, between-group contrasts, coordinate tables and figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Limitations. Thus all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based parametric n-back working memory paradigm (executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM96 group map, Talairach coordinates, tables/figures) and within-group task contrasts across load levels (0B,1B,2B,3B). Participants are healthy controls (within-group contrasts reported). Results are reported as coordinates and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations.

Study is an empirical fMRI investigation of working memory (n-back), an executive function domain, reporting within-subject, within-group voxelwise task contrasts (n-back vs rest and paired [Before2nd] vs [After] chewing) with group-level random-effects analyses and tables/figures of whole-brain activations (coordinates reported). Methods, results, and discussion are present; the imaging analysis is voxelwise whole-brain (normalization, smoothing, group-level paired t-tests). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise activation maps (whole-brain composite maps and Talairach-transformed group maps), ROI analyses, and time courses; includes within-group contrasts (No-HF vs No-LF, nonmatch vs match) and reports coordinates/figures. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. All required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met; no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references and appears complete.

Full text is incomplete: provided content contains only references and bibliographic metadata, not the article’s introduction, methods, results, or discussion. The title indicates an fMRI study of response inhibition, so I5 (fMRI task-based study) and I6 (inhibition within executive-function domains) appear to be met based on title/metadata. However, I cannot verify I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical map), I8 (at least one within-group task contrast), or I10 (clear reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures/text) because core methods/results are missing. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are demonstrably met from the available content. Decision: EXCLUDED due to incomplete full text; eligible inclusion criteria I7 and I8 not verifiable without full manuscript.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study of spatial working memory (executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (ANCOVA) and both a priori search volumes and an exploratory whole-brain search with corrected thresholds; results are presented as stereotaxic coordinates and subtraction contrasts. Within-group task contrasts are reported (spatial span vs visuomotor control; spatial manipulation vs control; spatial manipulation vs span). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (n=5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses task-based fMRI of an executive function (working memory for order) and reports within-group task contrasts in healthy adults (I5, I6, I8, I9 satisfied), all reported analyses were conducted within predefined ROIs (four 12mm spheres) rather than as voxelwise, whole-brain group-level maps. The paper does not present voxelwise whole-brain activation results or coordinates/tables for a whole-brain contrast, so it fails inclusion criterion I7 and therefore meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The full text reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level statistical maps (mixed-effects FLAME analyses) and provides within-group contrasts (e.g., 2-back>1-back, 2-back>0-back, 1-back>0-back) for both MDD patients and healthy controls. Results include cluster thresholds, Z-statistics and coordinate tables/figures. Although acquisition used 24 axial slices, analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-limited. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function task (letter fluency) in ALS patients and controls, with whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses and within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline). Results are reported as thresholded group maps and cluster coordinates in tables/figures. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control using a stop‑signal paradigm (executive function: inhibition). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with within-group contrasts (SST vs NST; UST vs NST), provides Talairach coordinates and figures, and includes methods, results, and discussion. Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based response inhibition paradigms (stop and go/no-go) that probe executive function (inhibition). The paper reports within-group ‘generic activation’ maps for controls and patients (activation vs control conditions) and describes voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Talairach-transformed FPQ and γ maps, voxelwise ANCOVA with permutation cluster tests), with coordinates and cluster tables. Partial slice coverage was used but the analyses were voxelwise and group-level maps are reported. Results are presented as within-group contrasts and coordinate tables/figures. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical PET activation study using the Tower of London planning task (executive function domain). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM) including within-group correlational contrasts of rCBF vs task complexity and categorical task-minus-rest contrasts for each group; results are presented as statistical parametric maps and coordinate tables. Participant groups include both Parkinson’s patients and healthy controls. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Tables — full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI of executive function (2-back working memory) with clinical groups, employing voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxelwise t-tests/ANOVAs) and reporting within-group task>fixation contrasts for each group. The paper provides complete methods, results, and discussion, and clearly describes clusterwise thresholding and voxelwise maps. All required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (fMRI executive task; working memory domain; voxelwise whole-brain analyses; within-group task contrasts reported; clinical participant groups included; results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not solely between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study using a Sternberg verbal working memory task (an established executive-function domain). The authors performed voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) contrasting task vs control within participants for encoding, maintenance, and retrieval periods, and reported whole-brain activation foci (tables/figures), despite restricting reporting to ROIs and having incomplete inferior cerebellar coverage. These analyses satisfy within-group task contrasts and voxelwise group maps required by the review. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task-based study of numerical Stroop/conflict processing, which assesses cognitive control/inhibition and conflict resolution, matching executive function domains. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with t and F contrasts and tables/coordinates for task contrasts (conflict vs nonconflict; error vs correct), satisfying within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults; results are reported as standard voxelwise activation tables and figures. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment of methods and group-level voxelwise findings. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using the counting Stroop (inhibition domain of executive function). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects analyses (incongruent > congruent contrast), presents within-group activation maps/tables/coordinates for both healthy and bipolar groups, and describes methods/results in full. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function whole-brain activation reporting. Sample size and medication status are noted as limitations but do not violate inclusion/exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (overt letter verbal fluency, a classical measure of executive initiation/selection). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GBAMs and voxelwise permutation testing) despite partial slice coverage, and presents within-group task contrasts (verbal fluency vs word repetition) for the placebo and ketamine conditions. Participants are healthy adults (eligible), and results are reported in the main text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and includes within-group contrasts). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that manipulates the central executive component of working memory using a number-subtraction task (meets I5). The task targets working memory/central executive executive-domain processes (meets I6). Imaging methods and analyses are whole-brain and voxelwise (SPM99 preprocessing, normalization, second-level random-effects one-sample t tests with voxelwise thresholds and cluster extent), and coordinates/figures/tables of activations are reported (meets I7 and I10). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (each subtraction condition vs baseline; high-demand vs low-demand; interaction contrasts) at group level (meets I8). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (meets I9). No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of saccadic inhibition (antisaccade and fixation vs prosaccade), an established executive function domain (inhibition). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level statistical maps (t maps) and voxelwise analyses with Bonferroni-corrected thresholds, and provides within-group task contrasts (inhibition vs prosaccade and main effects) for both controls and patients, including activation maps and coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and empirical). Therefore it meets I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included.

This is a PET study with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) comparing syntactically complex (SO) versus simple (OS) sentences within groups; coordinates and within-group contrasts are reported. However, the study’s primary focus is language/syntactic processing and individual differences in working memory and processing speed, not an executive function or cognitive control task per se. Although working memory was measured as an individual-difference variable, the experimental task is a plausibility judgment for sentence comprehension rather than a task designed to probe established executive domains (working memory task paradigms, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Inclusion criteria met: I7, I8, I9, I10. Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task), which falls squarely within executive function (inhibition). The paper reports subject-level SS vs SE contrasts, ROI analyses, and whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group-level voxelwise comparison and whole-brain results reported, even if some findings used uncorrected thresholds). At least one within-group task contrast (SS > SE) was computed and reported in effect-size histograms and regression analyses, satisfying a within-group activation contrast. Participants include a clinical sample (cocaine-dependent men), which is acceptable. Reporting includes voxelwise whole-brain results (tables/description) and coordinate-based results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back) in adolescents and adults and reports within-group task contrasts (task vs fixation) and task-domain comparisons (I5, I6, I8, I9, I10 satisfied). However, the paper uses a region-of-interest (ROI)-based analysis approach (spherical ROIs derived from prior literature) to interrogate task effects, and the reported results are from these ROI statistics. Although single-subject voxelwise GLMs were estimated, the group-level results presented are ROI-based rather than group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain statistical maps. The manuscript does not present a voxelwise group-level task activation map or whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses that would meet I7. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no voxelwise group maps) and must be excluded.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study using a stop-signal task (inhibition — an executive function), with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and within-group contrasts (successful vs failed stop trials) reported in tables/figures and text. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text, and the study provides coordinates and group-level SPM results. Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (fixed-effect in Experiment 1; random-effect in Experiment 2) using SPM, with thresholding and cluster inference and peak coordinates provided. Within-group task contrasts (working memory task versus control) are reported and used in the group analyses. Results are presented as voxelwise subtraction images and coordinate tables/figures. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes complete methods, results and discussion. Therefore it fulfills all inclusion criteria for task activation meta-analysis.

This paper reports an empirical event-related fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/No-go), which is an executive function task (inhibition). It used whole-brain coverage (29 slices covering the entire brain), performed group-level voxelwise analyses with SPM97, and reports within-group task contrasts (Go vs baseline, No-go vs baseline, No-go vs Go, Go vs No-go) with tables and figures of activations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based N-back working-memory paradigm in postmenopausal women. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (3-back > 0-back) with SPM2, corrected p-values and MNI coordinates/cluster extents, satisfying requirement for a within-group task contrast and whole-brain activation maps. The task falls within executive function (working memory) and participant group is acceptable. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be included for meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level mixed-model ANOVAs and within-group/load main effects and contrasts (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), including reporting of statistical maps, clusters, and coordinate-based results. Although acquisition covered 26 contiguous slices (partial-brain coverage), analyses were voxelwise and thus meet the partial-brain allowance. Within-group task contrasts (load main effects) are reported for at least one group, and results are described in text/tables/figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly examines volitional inhibitory control of breathing. The paradigm is task-based (15-s breath holds) and the authors relate findings to response-inhibition networks. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM group results, FWE-corrected maps and tables of coordinates). At least one within-group task contrast (breath hold vs baseline/implicit baseline, modelled in SPM) is presented. Participants are healthy adults (within-group results given). Results are reported as figures and tabulated coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function/inhibition domain meta-analysis and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study (N-Back and AX-CPT) examining working memory and inhibition in schizophrenia. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain ANOVAs with cluster-size correction and provides tables/coordinates of activated regions. Within-group task effects are reported (load main effects for N-Back; cue-type and cue×scan effects for AX-CPT) and planned contrasts confirmed effects in each group. Participants include a clinical schizophrenia sample and healthy controls. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI of verbal working memory (n-back) in healthy adults, with group-level voxelwise analyses and a within-group task contrast (n-back vs sensorimotor control). The paper describes whole-brain multislice acquisition, voxelwise sinusoidal regression and regression analyses relating fMRI response power to reaction time, and reports peak coordinates for activations. These satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group contrasts). Note: the provided full text appears incomplete (title and abstract/metadata only), so I flagged fulltext_incomplete=true and applied the inclusion criteria based on the available abstract and metadata.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly examines short-term storage and comparison of auditory durations—a working memory operation within executive function. The paper reports a within-group contrast (discrimination minus identification) analyzed at the group level using voxelwise SPM99 procedures with whole-brain coverage, and presents voxel coordinates and activation figures/clusters. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the full text provided. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level activation maps for mental arithmetic. The task includes a working-memory component (retaining intermediate results) and thus falls within an executive-function domain (working memory). The paper reports within-group contrasts (active math vs control) for musicians, non-musicians, and all subjects combined, with voxelwise random-effects analyses and figures/tables of coordinates. Results are whole-brain (composite activation maps and coordinate tables) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes an established executive function paradigm (oculomotor delayed response — a spatial working memory task). Voxelwise, group-level and within-group task contrasts are reported (one-sample t-tests and voxelwise between-group t-tests; ODR vs visually guided saccade within-group contrasts are presented). Although acquisition had limited slice coverage, the analyses were voxelwise (whole-brain evidence criterion accepts partial-brain acquisition), and results are reported in figures and tables. therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back), an executive function. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (group t-maps for 1-, 2-, 3-back vs 0-back) and provides within-group task contrasts for patient and control groups, with whole-brain voxelwise thresholding and reported peak coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visuospatial working memory (mental rotation), which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses with statistical thresholds and coordinates transformed to Talairach space, and multiple within-group task contrasts (rotation vs identity; simultaneous vs successive) reported across the whole brain. Participants are a healthy adult sample. Results are reported in the text with coordinates and detailed contrasts. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based 2-back verbal working memory paradigm (executive function). It reports group-level voxelwise SPM99 whole-brain analyses with coordinates and cluster statistics (BBR correlations with rCBF), and within-group task analyses (2-back vs reference and performance correlations). Results are reported as Talairach/MNI coordinates. All inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of a working memory (executive function) task comparing structured vs unstructured sequences. The paper reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected, peaks and coordinates reported) and supplementary ROI analyses; behavioral and control experiments are included. All required inclusion criteria are met (fMRI task-based executive function; working memory domain; whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with reported coordinates; within-group contrasts; participant group reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and experimental procedures).

This is an empirical PET study of a working-memory task (face matching) with task-based, within-group contrasts (task vs rest) reported separately for young and older groups. Analyses were voxelwise whole-brain SPM contrasts with reported thresholding and coordinates, results presented in tables/figures, and detailed methods/results/discussion present in the provided full text. The study directly assesses an executive function domain (working memory) and provides group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (within-group contrasts). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group activation contrasts). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (working memory, n-back) in patients and controls. It reports within-group 2-back > 0-back voxelwise contrasts for both groups and group-level random-effects analyses with whole-brain coverage and coordinates/tables of activation maxima. Results are presented as voxelwise statistical maps (SPM/SnPM) and reported in tables/figures. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visual spatial working memory (an executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (ANOVA on voxelwise BOLD time courses, FDR correction, clusters, Talairach normalization) and presents within-group task contrasts (main effect of time for short and long delay trials; repeated-measures ANOVAs across subjects). Participant group (healthy adults, N=16) is reported. Whole-brain voxelwise results are described and tabulated/figured. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) that reports voxelwise whole-brain group analyses and within-group contrasts. The paper presents voxelwise ANOVAs, planned within-group contrasts (e.g., combination > object/location in young adults), Talairach coordinates, figures, and tables of activations. Although only 21 axial slices were acquired, the analyses are voxelwise (partial-brain acquisition is allowed). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function) that reports within-group and between-group voxelwise group analyses using SPM2 with whole-brain, random-effects contrasts (e.g., VT>FT, FT>FIX). Results are reported in tables and figures, with FDR correction described, and include within-group contrasts for Controls and PTSD. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory in healthy adults (meets I5, I6), and it used within-subject task contrasts (encoding/maintenance vs baseline) and group-level summary statistics on those contrasts (meets I8 and I9). However, the paper does not present a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or coordinates for within-group activations; primary results are reported as counts of suprathreshold voxels within an a priori mask and focal ROI analyses rather than voxelwise group maps. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (no voxelwise group-level activation map reported) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports ROI/aggregate voxel-count metrics without providing voxelwise group statistical maps). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a rule-based go/nogo (ocular baseball) task that directly probes executive functions—specifically inhibition and rule-guided decision-making. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (individual subject contrasts and group-level SPM99 analyses with voxelwise thresholds and cluster extent) and provides coordinates and figures for activations (e.g., right VLPFC, SPL, FEF, SEF). Tasks fall within established executive domains (inhibition/rule processing). Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts (decided-nogo vs always-nogo; decided-go vs always-go) are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment of criteria. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and none of the exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function domain) with healthy participants. This is an empirical fMRI study using an n-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). Multiple within-group task contrasts are presented (e.g., retrieval with shift vs control; retrieval with shift vs retrieval without shift; continuous shift vs retrieval without shift), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Participants are a healthy adult sample, which is acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (integration vs segregation) — an executive function domain. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects voxelwise ANOVAs and voxelwise conjunction contrasts), with within-group task contrasts (IN vs SG vs MO vs RO) and coordinates/tables/figures (Table 1, Figures). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (1-back) — an executive function domain — reporting voxelwise, whole-brain mixed-effects analyses and within-group contrasts (sustained and transient activity; task vs baseline). It provides group-level, voxelwise statistical maps (thresholds, cluster sizes) and reports results in text/tables/figures for younger and older adult groups. The full text includes Intro, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group contrasts). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and is included.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back), an executive function, reporting voxelwise within-group 2-back vs baseline contrasts and group-level activation maps (second-level SPM analyses). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion; coordinates and whole-brain activation patterns are provided and ROI time-series were extracted for SEM, but voxelwise activation results and within-group contrasts are explicitly reported. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task, domain, voxelwise whole-brain analysis, within-group contrasts, and reporting format. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI of spatial working memory (an executive function domain), includes whole-brain voxelwise group- and within-group (WM>AV and WM>PV) contrasts, and provides voxelwise results described across the text (with cluster thresholds and coordinates). Participants include clinical (schizophrenia/schizoaffective) and healthy volunteer groups. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study of cognitive flexibility (task switching), meeting the review objective. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (62,980-voxel mask; voxelwise regressions and group t maps with cluster correction) and presents results in figures and tables (Table 1, Figs. 1–3). Within-group contrasts/analyses are reported (trial-evoked switch vs repeat paired t tests and voxelwise regressions of pretrial signal predicting RT performed within subjects and tested at group level). Participants and methods are described in full. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and is suitable for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based paradigms of working memory (object and spatial WM), which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain, group-level statistical maps (Z-maps transformed to Talairach space, corrected thresholds) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., object vs spatial delays, task vs sensorimotor control). Participants and methods are described and results are reported at the group and single-subject level. Reporting includes voxelwise maps and region-wise analyses consistent with inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that parametrically manipulates working-memory demands during a grammaticality-judgment task. It directly assesses working memory (an established executive function domain) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (group maps, cluster thresholds, MNI coordinates). Within-group task contrasts and linear-effect contrasts (distance effects within Movement and Binding conditions; grammatical trials versus baseline) are reported. Participants are healthy adults. Results and analyses (methods, results, discussion) are fully present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory (Sternberg variant), addressing executive function (access/evaluation in WM). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level random-effects analyses (paired t-tests across N=8) with coordinates and time-series, and includes within-group task contrasts (negative vs positive responses). Participants are a within-group healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back CPT) in healthy adults, reporting voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses contrasting 2-back vs 0-back (a within-group task contrast). Results include coordinates and cluster statistics (BA10) and methods indicate whole-brain voxelwise analysis. Thus the paper meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive control/dual-task processing in healthy adults. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-head analyses (e.g., DM>SM, SM>SP), Time×Group and Time×Group×Condition interactions, and provides coordinates and statistical maps in the text/tables. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes an established executive-function task (2-back working memory) and reports within-group, voxelwise group analyses. Methods describe whole-brain GLM analyses with random-effects group maps and FDR thresholding; contrasts include 2-back vs 0-back (within-group task contrast). Results provide Talairach coordinates and tables of activated regions, satisfying reporting of whole-brain voxelwise results. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based antisaccade (inhibition) and ocular motor delayed response (working memory) paradigms that clearly probe executive function. The paper reports a voxelwise, group-level one-sample t test (whole-brain clustered map) comparing volitional saccade blocks vs fixation (task-evoked activation map), and reports within-group task effects (regions showing increased BOLD during volitional saccades) as well as group comparisons. Tasks fall within established executive domains (inhibition, working memory). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses and voxelwise thresholding/cluster correction are described. A within-group task contrast (task vs fixation) is reported (main effect of task), and clinical and healthy groups are included. The full text (background, methods, results, figures, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study of inhibitory control/movement selection (executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses including whole-brain cluster-corrected results and within-group contrasts (isolated index flexion vs full-hand flexion; rest vs movement). The sample (10 healthy adults) provides within-group contrasts. Results are reported in the text with coordinates/clusters and methods (SPM99) for whole-brain and basal ganglia ROI analyses. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based Stroop paradigm (inhibition/cognitive control), reporting voxelwise, whole-brain group-level activation maps (incongruent vs congruent) for both patients and controls, and within-group contrasts. The methods explicitly describe voxel-by-voxel t-tests, voxelwise multiple regression, Talairach normalization, and tables/figures of activations. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activations (I5–I10). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study that directly investigates task switching (cognitive flexibility), an executive function domain, using a task-based paradigm. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (voxelwise t-tests averaged across 16 participants, thresholded and assessed with Friston–Worsley correction), and presents within-group task contrasts (task switch vs task repetition). Although slice coverage was limited (seven slices), the analyses are voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted. Results are reported in figures and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and thus appears complete for screening purposes. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that investigates spatial working memory (an established executive function domain). It used whole-brain acquisition and reports voxelwise group analyses (ROI-based and normalized group-average/t-maps with coordinates and tables). Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., delay-period contrasts [Delayfilled, Delayunfilled], lateralized contrasts), and results are reported for a within-group healthy adult sample. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study reports voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (SPM2) with within-group task contrasts (3-back vs OFF) and provides tables/figures with coordinates. Participant sample (healthy male social drinkers) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a working memory (N-back) task (executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxelwise regression, cluster-level permutation tests) and presents within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline; load and repetition parametric contrasts), with results in figures/tables. Partial slice coverage (21 near-axial slices) is present but the analysis is voxelwise and thus meets I7 per criteria. Participants are healthy adults (I9). Whole-brain results are reported in tables and figures (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based PET study of the Stroop paradigm (inhibition/cognitive control), reporting group-level, voxelwise canonical Z-score eigenimages derived from NPAIRS/CVA (rSPMs) and thresholded statistics. The study presents a within-group task contrast (congruent vs incongruent) and a 12-class model capturing practice effects, with whole-brain PET acquisition and voxelwise preprocessing/normalization. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and described in text/figures/tables. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study reports an event-related fMRI study using the Sternberg working memory task (an established executive function domain). It includes within-group voxelwise group-level analyses (6-digit vs 2-digit load), whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction, and results are reported in text/figures. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of interference control (numerical Stroop), directly addressing inhibition (an executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM2 analyses including within-group contrasts (distance and congruity effects), baseline contrasts, conjunction analysis, and tables/coordinates of whole-brain activations. Participant groups include a clinical sample (MCI) and controls. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and activation tables, indicating completeness. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) apply. Thus the study satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based paradigms (N-back, WCST, CPT) that probe executive functions (working memory, cognitive flexibility, vigilance). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (2-back > 0-back one-sample t-test and regression analyses using SPM2) with tables/figures of activation peaks and corrected results, satisfying a within-group task contrast. The sample is a participant group (healthy young adults) which is acceptable. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (working memory manipulation) using a modified Sternberg paradigm. The full text reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs) and provides coordinates/tables and figures for within-group contrasts (encoding vs baseline; alphabetize vs forward) and between-group contrasts. Analyses were performed with SPM2 across the whole brain with familywise error correction reported for within-group maps and voxelwise group comparisons reported with coordinate tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). The full text reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (main effect of task reported with whole-brain FWE correction) as well as within-group contrasts (e.g., 2-back > 0-back and 0-back vs fixation) for both patients and controls. Partial reliance on small-volume correction for some DLPFC tests is present, but whole-brain voxelwise results are reported and tabulated. The methods, results, and discussion are complete in the provided full text. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, random-effects group analyses (contrast maps, cluster-level correction) and whole-brain coverage, and presents within-group task contrasts (e.g., verbal vs non-verbal, task>baseline). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported in tables and figures. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I5-I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion allowing verification of voxelwise group contrasts.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain task contrasts relevant to executive function. The tasks include spatial working memory (an established executive function domain) and sustained spatial attention/vigilance. The paper presents group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM), reports coordinates and statistical maps for contrasts such as WM delay vs control and attention delay vs control, and performs laterality contrasts (attend-right vs attend-left). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory and vigilance domains), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinates reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (healthy adult participant group within-group contrasts reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and described in text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical PET study reporting task-based activation during executive/cognitive tasks (WCST and RPM). It includes within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (task minus control) using SPM and voxel-by-voxel analyses, with whole-brain coverage and reported statistical maps/tables. WCST is a canonical executive function (working memory/cognitive flexibility) satisfying the executive-domain requirement. Results are presented as group-level activation maps and tables/figures, and full methods, results, and discussion are provided in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of the cognitive process 'refreshing', framed as a minimal executive-function/working-memory component. It reports within-group, voxelwise random-effects contrasts (e.g., Refresh > Repeat; Face > Scene) using whole-brain SPM2 analyses and group-level cluster results with coordinates and thresholds. Participants were a within-group sample of healthy adults. The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (task maps onto executive/WM processes), I7 (group-level voxelwise/whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control using a stop-signal paradigm (executive function: inhibition). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task details, subjects, image acquisition, analysis), Results (group-level voxelwise activation maps, Bonferroni-corrected voxelwise threshold, coordinates table), and Discussion. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (GO ONLY vs GO/STOP; parametric STOP-likelihood analysis; correct vs incorrect STOP trials) at the group level using voxelwise statistical maps and provides coordinates and figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an n-back working-memory task (an executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 random-effects, voxelwise t-tests with coordinates reported), within-group task contrasts (e.g., control group activation across 1-back to 3-back and VOI analyses), and results are presented as coordinates and statistical maps. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study that includes a canonical executive function task (Go/No-go) probing response inhibition, reported as within-subject, within-group contrasts (No-go vs Go). Imaging used whole-brain, voxelwise, random-effects analysis (SPM2) with reported statistical maps, tables, and figures (coordinates and cluster results), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Other tasks are secondary but do not preclude inclusion. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of analyses. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Stroop task (inhibition), reporting within-group voxelwise contrasts (incongruent > congruent and incongruent > control) with group-level paired t-tests and Talairach coordinates/tables. Methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and statistical analysis; results list activated clusters and coordinates. Participants are native Japanese adults (healthy sample). Thus the study meets all meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task domain (inhibition), imaging modality (fMRI), whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and within-group contrasts; no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text content provided is limited to title, abstract, and metadata only (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract the study is an empirical PET task study of working memory in schizophrenia, meeting I5 (PET task-based), I6 (working memory task), I8 (within-group task vs fixation contrast), and I9 (clinical and control groups). However, the full text is not available to confirm critical inclusion criterion I7 (that at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical map/analysis was reported) or I10 (format of whole-brain results). Because I7 cannot be verified from the abstract alone and the review requires explicit whole-brain voxelwise results, I cannot confirm all required inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are clearly met from the abstract. Therefore I must exclude due to incomplete full text and inability to confirm whole-brain voxelwise analyses.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task-based Stroop switching paradigm that directly assesses cognitive control/executive function. The paper reports group-level voxelwise spatial F maps and contrasts (instruction-related: color naming > word reading; response-related: incongruent > congruent), with Talairach coordinates and voxel clusters reported, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting and coordinate reporting. Within-group task contrasts are explicitly presented and correlated with behavioral Stroop effects. Participants are a within-group healthy sample (meets participant flexibility). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (delayed-recognition), which falls squarely within executive function domains (working memory). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps (mapwise analyses, random-effects t-tests, cluster correction) and within-group task contrasts (task vs fixation; object vs spatial). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study that directly assesses response inhibition (an executive function) using task-based paradigms (manual Stroop and imitation-inhibition). It reports within-group, voxelwise contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) at the group level with whole-brain SPM analyses and thresholded activation maps and coordinate tables. Acquisition covered the whole brain (slice coverage described) and results are reported in tables/figures/text (Talairach coordinates). Participants were healthy adult subjects (within-group contrasts reported). The paper therefore satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain fMRI executive-function activation. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is an empirical study). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (Sternberg task) in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level activation contrasts. The paper presents within-group contrasts (e.g., average encoding vs implicit baseline; load-dependent linear contrasts) tested with random-effects one-sample t-tests and reports whole-brain corrected results (tables and surface renderings). Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based executive function (working memory) fMRI, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This PET study administered an auditory continuous performance task (a vigilance task) in a group of 66 healthy adults, so it meets I5 (PET, task-based) and I6 (task within executive domain: vigilance). However, the full text reports interregional covariance/connectivity analyses (Metabolic Associativity Matrix and voxel-wise correlation maps of regional metabolism across subjects) rather than any within-group task activation contrast (e.g., task > baseline) or task-evoked voxelwise statistical activation maps. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity-only analyses without a task activation map). Inclusion criteria I7 (whole-brain, task-evoked voxelwise map) and I8 (within-group task contrast) are not satisfied, so the study cannot be included for a meta-analysis of task activations.

This study reports original task-based fMRI data probing executive functions (motor response inhibition and motor timing), includes within-group task contrasts (activation vs baseline) and presents voxelwise, group-level analyses (FPQ maps, permutation tests) with reported coordinates and regional/voxelwise effects. Although imaging used limited slice coverage (15 non-contiguous planes), the paper performs voxelwise whole-brain-style analyses and reports coordinate tables/GBAMs, which satisfies the meta-analysis’ allowance for partial-brain acquisition and coordinate reporting. Participant groups include adolescents and adults and within-group contrasts are reported for both. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly investigates cognitive control/executive-function processes (maintaining intentions in working memory and evaluating actions) using a within-group task contrast (inconsistent vs. consistent actions). The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (voxelwise ANOVAs with reported peak coordinates across multiple brain regions) alongside ROI analyses. Although imaging used a limited number of slices (partial-brain coverage), voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and peak coordinates are reported, satisfying partial-brain voxelwise analysis requirements. Participants are healthy adults, and results are reported at the group level. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based verbal working memory paradigm (working memory = executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise activation contrasts (e.g., EAR > NO-MEMORY, EAR > EYE) with whole-brain analyses and cluster thresholds, and describes random-effects group statistics and β-series connectivity; coordinates and surface maps are reported. The contrasts are within-group task contrasts. Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be included.

This is an empirical PET activation study using a task-based paradigm (Hayling Test) that directly probes executive functions (verbal initiation and suppression). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise statistical parametric mapping analyses (SPM) with within-group contrasts (Hayling part A vs reading, part B vs reading, and A vs B). Although the scanner had a limited field-of-view (notably excluding the cerebellum), analyses were voxelwise and therefore satisfy the partial-brain allowance. Participants were healthy adults (acceptable per I9). Results are described in the text and figures (activation foci and Brodmann areas), meeting reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so is complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an established executive function domain) that reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level (random-effects) task contrasts (e.g. Space>NonSpace; AlloSpace–EgoSpace) using whole-brain SPM2 analyses with FDR correction and MNI coordinates/figures. Participants are a within-group healthy sample. Whole- brain results are reported in text, tables and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it meets I5–I10 and none of E3–E6.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (stop-signal task) with healthy adults. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2) with family-wise error correction and coordinates for activations (group-level contrasts such as pre-SS vs pre-SE). The task falls within the executive function domain (inhibition). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Only an abstract-style summary is provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the available text, the study used task-based fMRI (I5 met). However, it is unclear whether the task qualifies as an executive function domain (I6 not confirmed — sequencing/motor preparation may not map cleanly to working memory/inhibition/cognitive flexibility/planning/vigilance/initiation), whether whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps are reported (I7 not confirmed), and whether a within-group task contrast is reported (I8 not confirmed). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on the abstract. Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be verified, I exclude this study pending full-text review.

This is an event-related fMRI Stroop study of cognitive control with healthy adults that reports within-group task contrasts and coordinate results, but all voxelwise statistical testing was conducted within an a priori ROI mask (BA 24/32, 8/9/46, 7/40) rather than as whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps. Therefore it does not provide qualifying whole-brain voxelwise activation results. Exclusion ID E3 applies (reports only ROI/masked analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task of executive control), I6 (inhibition/cognitive control domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (eligible participant group), I10 (results reported with coordinates/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level task-evoked map; analyses confined to ROIs). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study of task switching (cognitive flexibility), meeting I5 and I6. The abstract reports whole-brain activations and group contrasts (main effects of predictability and task switching vs performing each task separately), consistent with voxelwise group-level task-evoked maps (I7) and within-group task contrasts (I8). Participant group is acceptable (I9) and results are reported in the text (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical. However, only title/abstract/metadata are provided here; the full article text (methods, full results, discussion, figures/tables) is not included, so fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is moderate.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly investigates initiation (an executive function domain) using an event-related paradigm. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM second-level random effects and thresholded maps), within-group task contrasts (e.g., planning internally-initiated vs rest; internally- vs externally-initiated planning), and provides coordinates and temporal SPM maps. Participants are a healthy adult sample (within-group contrasts reported). Reporting includes whole-brain results and ROI checks but is not limited to ROI-only analyses. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back), an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain second-level analyses (one-sample and two-sample SPM99 t-tests) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster corrections and provides coordinate tables. Within-group contrasts are reported (load effects: [2-back>0-back] for verbal and spatial sessions) for both patient and control groups. Participants include clinical (schizophrenia) and control samples. Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a resting-state FDG-PET study that compares regional metabolism between OCD patients and controls and correlates metabolic rates with neuropsychological test scores. It does not report any task-evoked, within-group voxelwise activation contrasts (no task-based PET/fMRI paradigm during imaging). Therefore it does not meet the review’s requirement for task-based executive-function activation maps. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/correlations with no within-group task activation contrast).
