This is an fMRI task study that includes an established executive-function task (incongruent color-word Stroop — inhibition/cognitive control) performed during scanning, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation contrasts. The paper provides within-group task contrasts (e.g., distraction-specific map (PD+HD)>(P+H), pain-specific contrasts (P−H), (PD−HD), and (PD−HD)>(P−H)), uses voxelwise SPM99 analyses across subjects, and reports whole-brain results in the text and tables. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy volunteers. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (random-effects), with whole-brain maps and Talairach/surface-based localizations. Within-group task contrasts are presented (Encode/Delay/Probe contrasts versus fixation and contrasts between delay conditions), and results are reported in tables and figures. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task study of verbal working memory (mPASAT) that reports within-group contrasts and voxel coordinates, but the statistical analyses are restricted to a predetermined set of ROIs (Brodmann areas) rather than providing a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation map. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain (or non-ROI-restricted) voxelwise task-evoked results (I7) and is excluded under exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory executive domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participants/groups acceptable), I10 (results reported with coordinates/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level map not provided; analyses confined to a priori ROIs).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a delayed-response working memory task (executive function). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses and within-group task contrasts (e.g., face > scrambled face; emotional > neutral), with tables/figures listing activation peaks. It therefore meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function task activation meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present and complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a working memory (N-back) paradigm (executive function). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise 2-back > 0-back second-level group analyses using SPM2 with whole-brain voxelwise thresholds and cluster results plus tables/coordinates. Participants are healthy older adults (acceptable). Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain executive function activation are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study using a Stroop color-word matching task (inhibition domain of executive function). The paper reports whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise group-level (random-effects) analyses contrasting incongruent vs. neutral conditions (within-group task contrast), with activation tables/figures and timecourse analyses. Participant groups and methodology are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function (PASAT; working memory) in MS patients and controls. Methods describe voxelwise whole-brain preprocessing and GLM analyses, with group-level random-effects and within-group one-sample t tests for task activation (P<0.005, cluster threshold), and between-group two-sample contrasts. Results present whole-brain activation tables with Talairach coordinates and figures. Neuropsychological and task performance data are provided. The paper therefore meets all required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study; within-group contrasts are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (nogo vs saccade), which falls within executive function (inhibition). It reports within-group voxelwise, mixed-effects group-level statistical maps (instruction and response contrasts) computed across subjects, with cluster correction. Although slice coverage was partial (axial slices to dorsal caudate/thalamus), analyses are whole-brain voxelwise within the imaged volume and therefore meet the partial-brain allowance. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion and provides coordinate/cluster tables and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using memory-guided saccade and a spatial working-memory task (working memory is an established executive function). Analyses used voxelwise methods (Fourier and regression) to produce statistical activation maps, group-level summaries (mean Talairach coordinates, volumes, group polar plots), and within-group contrasts versus baseline/fixation. Partial-brain coverage (frontal, parietal, dorsal occipital) is acceptable per protocol. Results include whole-brain voxelwise maps, coordinates, and figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, figures, references).

This is an event-related fMRI study of task switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility) that reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects statistical maps (switch vs stay contrasts) with coordinates and thresholding; it also includes within-group task contrasts (switch>stay) for healthy participants. Partial slice coverage (20 slices) was used but voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a Go/NoGo paradigm that probes response inhibition (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-group voxelwise one-sample t-tests for both abstinent heroin-dependent (AHD) and healthy control (HC) groups, group-level voxelwise between-group contrasts, and whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction; results are presented as activation maps and tables of coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as maps/coords). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an H2(15)O PET study using a task-based N-back working memory paradigm (executive function). It reports voxelwise, group-level SPM99 analyses (2-back minus 0-back) for within-group contrasts in both healthy controls and schizophrenic patients, with whole-brain activation maps, coordinates, and figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Thus all inclusion criteria for task modality, executive-domain task, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, within-group contrasts, participant groups, and reporting of whole-brain results are met. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study measuring brain activation during simultaneous interpreting, which involves verbal working memory and cognitive control processes. The study uses group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM96) and reports within-group contrasts (SI vs shadowing) comparing task against an active control, with results described in text and figures. Participants are a valid group (professional interpreters). All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a task-based fMRI study of sustained attention (vigilance), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses and within-group task contrasts (novel and practice blocks vs. baseline) for both cocaine and control groups. Methods, results, and group- and within-group activation maps/analyses are reported, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (delayed item recognition for letters) with a within-group, voxelwise second-level analysis. It tests WM load (set size) and reports whole-brain multivariate linear modeling and voxelwise GLM results (group-level), with figures and ROI follow-ups. The task clearly falls within the executive function domain (working memory). Results are presented as group-level voxelwise maps/plots (not ROI-only), and the contrast of task/delay versus implicit baseline and set-size effects are within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive flexibility/task switching using a Stroop/reverse-Stroop paradigm. This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based cognitive control paradigm (occluded target switching visual search) that probes executive functions (working memory, cognitive flexibility/switching, response preparation). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of inhibition (Go/Nogo) in schizophrenia that directly addresses executive function/cognitive control. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete). It includes within-group task contrasts (e.g., Nogo–Go, Go/Cue–Go/Noncue, Cued-Nogo–Uncued-Nogo) and reports task-effect activations (task main effects) and correlations, satisfying within-group contrast requirement. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visuospatial working memory (a canonical executive function subdomain: working memory). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (including permutation-based cluster inference), presents within-group task contrasts (encoding and recognition vs baseline/fixation), and provides tables of coordinates for activated regions. Participants (pre-menopausal women and matched controls) are acceptable per inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so content appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This is an empirical fMRI study of task-switching (cognitive flexibility), reporting within-group task contrasts (switch vs repeat) and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (group t-tests on normalized beta-maps) that identify a left superior parietal region. The paper contains complete methods, results, and discussion enabling extraction of task-evoked activation loci. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task-based, whole-brain, within-group study of a visuomotor tracking/motor-learning task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts: tracking vs rest and learning-related contrasts), I9 (healthy participant group within-group results), I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that investigates response inhibition using somatosensory go/nogo tasks (executive function domain: inhibition). This study reports task-based fMRI using a go/no-go variant probing inhibition and timing (executive function/cognitive control). Participant groups (ADHD, unaffected siblings, controls) are reported and any group is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not limited to between-group contrasts. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none.

This is an fMRI task-based study using the n-back working memory paradigm (an established executive function domain). Acquisition covered contiguous axial slices and results are described in methods, results, tables and figures. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). This is an empirical fMRI study using a task that probes visuospatial working memory (an established executive function domain). At least one within-group task contrast is presented (experimental spatial conditions vs. table task). Participants are a within-group (healthy adult) sample. This is a task-based PET study of executive function (planning) using a modified Tower of London paradigm (I5,I6). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study of a two-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (image acquisition, GLM), Results (voxelwise activations, tables, figures) and Discussion, so the article is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are violated. This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (semantic event sequencing/planning). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps are described and displayed; between-group contrasts and functional connectivity are also reported. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based n-back working memory paradigm (an executive-function task). This is an event-related fMRI study using a Stroop color-word task, which assesses cognitive control/inhibition (executive function). Results are presented as whole-brain composite maps and ROI tables/coordinates. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (delayed item recognition), which is an established executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise preprocessing and second-level GLM/CVA analyses and presents thresholded spatial maps and tables of local maxima (coordinates). The design includes within-group, task-related contrasts (load-dependent task effects computed at first-level and analyzed separately by age group at second-level), and results are reported for each participant group (young and elder). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This PET study reports voxelwise, group-level task contrasts that probe conditional movement selection based on arbitrary visual cues — a form of cognitive control/selection (executive function). It includes within-group contrasts (conditional vs. power+precision and movement vs. rest), whole-brain voxelwise analysis with reported peak coordinates, and meets reporting requirements. Participants are healthy adults and the imaging modality (PET) is acceptable. The task maps onto executive processes (stimulus-response selection/cognitive flexibility/selection) relevant to the meta-analysis objective. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/coordinates) is provided, enabling extraction of activation coordinates and contrasts.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the CPT-IP (a sustained attention/vigilance task), reporting within-group contrasts (CPT-IP vs control) and group composite voxelwise t-maps with voxel-by-voxel comparisons and cluster-based multiple-comparison correction. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (vigilance/executive domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based PASAT that targets working memory/attention (executive function). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Study is appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/NoGo), an established executive function (inhibition). This is an empirical fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task (an executive function: planning). This is an event-related fMRI study that directly assesses cognitive control/conflict (Stroop and Simon interference tasks) using task-based paradigms. This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control (task-switching/cognitive flexibility) with healthy adult participants. This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a working-memory (n-back) manipulation, which is an established executive function domain. This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based within-group contrasts (Melody Discrimination vs button-press control; Harmony Discrimination vs control; Melody Listening vs rest) that probe processes requiring working memory/monitoring and error detection (executive-type demands). This is a task-based fMRI study of action planning that directly manipulates and tests planning processes (an executive domain listed in I6: planning). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that assesses working memory (an established executive function domain) in concussed athletes and controls. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of task switching (verbal fluency alternating vs non-switching) assessing cognitive flexibility/executive control. It reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level SPM analyses (thresholds, cluster criteria), within-group contrasts (S > NS; SC > OS; interactions) and provides coordinate tables/figures. Healthy adult participants are included. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, tables and references, so it is complete and suitable for meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (working memory digit-sorting). The full text describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxel-by-voxel regression, reported clusters with Talairach coordinates), within-group task contrasts (condition-related effects across 3-,4-,5-digit conditions and main effects), and reports results in text and tables/figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present, and the study therefore meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI during an N-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper describes voxelwise SPM analyses of BOLD activation (2B vs 0B contrast), generation of subject contrast maps and group-level analyses, and reports peak coordinates and statistics for genotype effects on task-related activation in prefrontal cortex. A within-group task contrast (2-back vs 0-back) is explicitly used; results are reported as voxelwise activation loci (with correction within an ROI but obtained from voxelwise SPM analyses) and coordinates are provided in the text and figure. Participants include healthy controls (and clinical samples elsewhere), and the within-group contrast in controls qualifies. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The full-text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete (API error). Based on the available title/metadata, the study examines PET FDOPA influx related to prefrontal processing of affective (emotional) stimuli rather than an executive function task. Therefore it does not meet the requirement to assess executive function/cognitive control (I5, I6). Because the full text is unavailable, I cannot confirm whether whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I7), a within-group task contrast (I8), or reporting format (I10) are present. No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the available information. Recommendation: exclude due to not meeting I5 and I6; full text incomplete prevents verification of other inclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study (1.5T) reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses of within-group task contrasts comparing normal vs malingered recognition responses. Although the primary task is recognition memory, the experimental manipulation and contrasts specifically target cognitive control processes (response suppression/inhibition, response generation, working memory/monitoring) during deceptive responding. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise SnPM paired t-test contrasts (NH vs MM; NCR vs MFA), provides clusterwise results in tables/figures, and conducts reaction-time regressions constrained to significant regions. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI assessing cognitive control/executive processes via deception-related inhibition/response control), I6 (involves executive domains—response inhibition and working memory/monitoring), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of executive function (interference suppression and response inhibition) using a task-based paradigm (combined flanker and go/no-go). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (incongruent > neutral; no-go > neutral) analyzed with SPM99 and random-effects group analyses. Results include whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and regression analyses, with coordinates and cluster reports, and separate within-group maps for children and adults. Partial-brain acquisition is acceptable under I7 because voxelwise analyses were performed. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive-function activation maps and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and detailed experimental procedures).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive control (modified flanker) reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts. The paper describes BOLD fMRI methods, SPM99 voxelwise contrasts (INC>CON, NOGO>CON and INC>NEU/NOGO>NEU), random-effects group analyses, and reports activation maps/tables and correlations. Participants (n=57 healthy adults) are acceptable. Results are presented in text, figures and tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (3T BOLD) that investigates Stroop-like inhibition paradigms (colour, number, shape), directly addressing the executive function domain of inhibition. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise first-level contrasts (congruent vs neutral; incongruent vs neutral) and a random-effects, second-level group analysis using SPM2, with whole-brain voxelwise results thresholded and coordinates reported in tables and text. Although ROI analyses are also performed, whole-brain voxelwise group maps and between-modality voxelwise comparisons are presented. Participant sample is a within-group (healthy adults). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (executive function) using a simple warned RT paradigm (inhibition domain). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (one-sample t-tests, random-effects models) with whole-brain coverage and tables of coordinates and thresholded voxelwise results. Contrasts include within-group comparisons (e.g., cued vs no-cued; short vs long SOA) suitable as task activation maps. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based continuous performance (vigilance) paradigm, which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (within-group vigilance>fixation contrasts for both schizophrenia and healthy control groups) with cluster-correction and presents maps/tables of activations. Participants include clinical and control groups. All required inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain within-group activation are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly tests deception (pretending to know) which requires intentional response manipulation and cognitive control, consistent with executive function/inhibition domains. The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; random-effects ANOVA) with coordinates and thresholding, and presents within-group task contrasts (e.g., Lie vs Truth, LN vs CR, FR vs CR). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported as voxelwise activation maps and peak coordinates in the text/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) using an event-related paradigm with distractors. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses and a random-effects group-level contrast (memory-delay correct trials in distractor-plus vs control), with thresholding and activation coordinates reported. At least one within-group task contrast is presented; participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not a review). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and the study is eligible for inclusion.

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study of attentional control/set-shifting (executive function domain: cognitive flexibility). It reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., extradimensional vs intradimensional shifts; reversals vs set change; true vs false feedback) and whole-brain analyses (FDR-corrected whole-brain results and tables of peak coordinates). Participants (n=16 healthy volunteers) underwent group-level random-effects analyses and results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (imaging acquisition, event modeling), Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (working memory, response selection/conflict). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts (e.g., Repeat-Unexpected vs Repeat-Expected; Refresh vs Repeat), with coordinates and ROI analyses. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a Stroop task (executive function: inhibition/cognitive control) with voxelwise, group-level random effects analyses reported (thresholded maps, cluster extent) and multiple within-group task contrasts (oddball vs baseline neutral; incongruent vs neutral; eligible vs ineligible). Partial slice coverage (10 slices) is present but the analyses are voxelwise at the group level, which qualifies under I7. Whole-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Behavioral and imaging results are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a Stroop inhibition paradigm (executive function) with group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses. The manuscript reports within-group task contrasts (group mean activation maps for Stroop subtests and an interference minus color-naming contrast), whole-brain voxelwise results (SPM{t} maps, thresholded and displayed), and also reports ROI-masked analyses; participants include clinical/behavioral groups (heavy marijuana smokers and controls). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study reports task-based fMRI of working memory (modified Sternberg), with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects maps; tables of coordinates and figures), and within-group task contrasts (e.g., maintenance-retrieval vs rest and first vs last retrieval sections; parametric modulation of exponential signal change). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps and coordinates. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for fMRI executive-function activation studies.

This is a task-based PET study of sustained attention/vigilance and selective target detection (executive domains). The full text reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses with thresholded statistical maps and MNI/atlas coordinates for whole-brain results (e.g., Z values and x,y,z locations). Within-group contrasts are reported (S vs NS, time-on-task covariate, interaction analyses), and behavioural/voxelwise results are described for the healthy participant group. The paper includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates none.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory/source monitoring (executive/monitoring processes). It reports voxelwise whole-brain group analyses (F-maps transformed to Talairach space) and provides peak coordinates and cluster results. The paper describes within-group condition contrasts (e.g., PW > ON or LR in young adults; separate analyses and comparisons reported for young and older groups), satisfying a within-group task contrast requirement. Participants and methods are described in full, and results/reports meet the criterion for coordinates/voxelwise results reported in text/tables. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly probes inhibitory control using antisaccade and nogo paradigms (executive function: inhibition). It reports within-group, voxelwise mixed-effects contrasts (e.g., anti_response > pro_response, pro_response > baseline) and provides group-level statistical maps, tables of coordinates, and figures. Although slice coverage was limited (axial slices to dorsal caudate), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted, which meets the allowance for partial-brain acquisition (I7). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample, and multiple within-group contrasts are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the record appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of attentional control/conflict (Simon and spatial Stroop), which falls within executive functions (inhibition/conflict). It reports voxelwise, random-effects group analyses (whole-brain contrasts: Simon Incongruent > Simon Congruent; Stroop Incongruent > Stroop Congruent), conjunction/disjunction and direct contrast maps, and describes cluster thresholds and peak locations (tables/figures). Within-group task contrasts are clearly reported for the healthy participant group. Results are presented as whole-brain activation maps and tables/figures rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an empirical fMRI task (auditory oddball) that indexes selective attention/vigilance, which falls within the listed executive function domains (vigilance). It includes within-group voxelwise contrasts (target vs non-target) and reports whole-brain group-level analyses with thresholding and tables/figures of coordinates (Table 4, Figs. 4–5). Participants are a non-clinical adult sample (acceptable). Full methods, results and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive processes (verbal response initiation and suppression), reporting group-level, voxelwise activation maps and within-group contrasts (response initiation vs control; response suppression vs control; suppression vs initiation). Although slice coverage was partial (14 non-contiguous planes), analyses were voxelwise and group GBAM results with coordinates are reported in tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion included).

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task (an established executive function domain: planning). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (cluster-level inference corrected across the whole brain) and presents activation results in figures and tables. Within-subject contrasts for planning and movement execution were computed and entered into random-effects group analyses, satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast. Participants are healthy adults but the review accepts any participant group. The full text includes introduction, methods (task paradigm, imaging, preprocessing, statistics), results, and discussion, so the provided full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly includes executive-function tasks (response selection/inhibition: Incompatible vs Compatible mapping; and Algorithm construal requiring response selection/inhibition). It reports within-group task contrasts (Incompatible>Compatible; Belief>Photo; task vs baseline) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses including random-effects group-level contrasts (SPM99, reported group results and peak coordinates). Partial-brain coverage (excluding bottom cerebellum) is noted but voxelwise group analyses are provided, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Therefore the study provides usable whole-brain executive-function activation contrasts for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study with group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (semantic task vs control) and reports whole-brain results. However, the experimental paradigm is a lexico-semantic association/decision task, not an explicit executive function/cognitive control task. Although the authors discuss possible working memory demands, the task was not designed to probe established executive domains (working memory was neither manipulated nor the primary target). Therefore the study does not meet I5 (task assesses executive function/cognitive control) and I6 (task falls within established EF domains). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete. Exclusion summary: excluded because I5 and I6 are not satisfied; other inclusion criteria (I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a go/no-go paradigm (inhibition) with group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts reported (performed errors vs correct, observed errors vs correct, etc.). Whole-brain coverage and voxelwise analyses are described and coordinate tables/figures are provided; ROI/SVC were used but whole-brain results are also reported. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (only ROI results, only connectivity/resting-state, only between-group contrasts, non-empirical) are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (executive function) in schizophrenia and healthy controls, using a Sternberg task (encoding, maintenance/manipulation, retrieval). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group- and within-group analyses (SPM2 preprocessing, random-effects second-level analyses), including within-group task contrasts (correct retrieval vs baseline) and between-group contrasts; results and coordinates are described. It therefore satisfies: task-based fMRI assessing executive function (I5), task within executive domains (working memory) (I6), whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I7), within-group task contrasts reported (I8), includes clinical and healthy participant groups (I9), and reports whole-brain results in text/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study using a task-based oddball paradigm that probes attentional control and working-memory updating (executive domains: vigilance/working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise one-sample t-test analyses (familywise error corrected) and within-group task contrasts (targets and novels vs implicit baseline) as well as parametric modulation by target/novel interval. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps and peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study reports task-based manipulations of working memory within sentence processing (dual-task and spacing manipulations) and examines BOLD activation with voxelwise, group-level SPM contrasts (whole-brain analyses and coordinate tables). It includes within-group task contrasts (e.g., transitivity vs inflectional morphology; grammatical category vs morphology) and reports SPM results and coordinates across the brain. Participants are healthy young adults, but any participant group is acceptable. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for executive-function domain (working memory), fMRI task paradigm, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures, references). Included criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is an event-related fMRI, task-based empirical study that directly examines language switching and its reliance on inhibitory/executive control. It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (e.g., language switching vs. non-switching; forward vs. backward switching) analyzed with SPM2 using random-effects and whole-brain voxelwise thresholds, and presents coordinates/tables and activation maps. The task probes executive domains (inhibition/cognitive flexibility) and participants (second-language learners) are acceptable per criteria. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied (fMRI task, executive domain, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, within-group contrasts, any participant group allowed, whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of selective attention and cognitive control (Stroop and oddball tasks), reporting within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g. Stroop-incongruency vs Stroop-congruency; Word-oddball vs Oddball control) with random-effects whole-brain analyses and coordinate tables/figures. The tasks map onto executive function domains (inhibition/attentional control). Group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps are described; methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Stroop task, which assesses inhibition/action-monitoring (executive function), satisfying I5 and I6. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses using SPM (fixed- and random-effects), and provides within-group task-versus-control contrasts (one-sample t-tests) for both patients and controls, meeting I7 and I8. Participant groups include clinical OCD patients and healthy controls, acceptable per I9. Whole-brain results are presented in figures and tables of coordinates, satisfying I10. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present; fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an event-related fMRI study using an emotional oddball task that probes executive control/inhibition and attention. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (voxel-wise t-maps and ANOVAs) and within-group contrasts (targets vs baseline; sad vs neutral distractors; Target-after-Sad vs Target-after-Neutral) for both MDD and control groups. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10) and no exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of semantic (category) verbal fluency that explicitly examines executive components (response inhibition, working memory, sustained attention) associated with paced vs. unpaced and overt vs. covert generation. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, cluster-corrected p<.05) and within-group task contrasts (word generation overall and condition contrasts versus control/saying “nothing”). Participant group is healthy adults (acceptable). Results are reported in text, tables, and figures; full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level task contrasts of tactile object discrimination that explicitly probe working-memory and discrimination processes. The paper reports within-group contrasts (P2 vs P1, P1 vs spheres, delay vs baseline), voxelwise statistical maps/coordinates with cluster- and voxel-level correction, and tables/figures of whole-brain activations. Participant group (healthy adults) is reported. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for task-based executive function activations.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for a task-based executive-function neuroimaging meta-analysis. It is an fMRI study using a cognitive control/inhibition paradigm (counting Stroop). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain mixed-effects analyses are reported (cluster-thresholded Z maps with peak coordinates reported in tables/figures). Crucially, within-group task contrasts (I–N Stroop contrast) are presented and contrasted between Trp and placebo conditions; results include whole-brain activation patterns and coordinates. The participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable under I9. The paper is an empirical task-evoked fMRI study (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore include in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI task study that explicitly examines cognitive control/executive processes during cooperative and competitive game play. Methods report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise thresholds and contrasts, including within-group contrasts (cooperation vs independent; competition vs independent). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported in figures/tables and described in the text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present, so fulltext is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based paradigm that probes executive function (sequencing/working memory initiation and manipulation via backward vs forward recitation). Group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses are reported (whole-brain voxelwise maps with cluster correction and Talairach coordinates), including within-group contrasts (REVERSE–FORWARD and task vs baseline) and practice-related within-group effects. Results are presented as figures and tables of coordinates. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task-based inhibition/cognitive control paradigm (ANT variant with incongruent vs congruent arrow and gaze stimuli). The paper reports within-group voxelwise random-effects contrasts (incongruent > congruent) for both neurotypical and autism groups, whole-brain analyses with FDR thresholding, and provides coordinates (Table 2) and figures of activation maps. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI, provides within-group contrasts, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (an executive function domain) using a within-subject emotional go/no-go paradigm. The paper reports voxelwise, random-effects whole-brain analyses (one-sample and paired-sample t tests) and regression analyses, with results described in tables and figures. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (e.g., positive distracter vs positive target; phase comparisons), and participant group (healthy premenopausal women) qualifies. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes executive function tasks (working memory STERN; also attention and associative memory). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (e.g., NT vs CT for working memory; TO vs RS for attention; AL vs SC and RE vs SC for associative memory). Group-level voxelwise maps were generated by combining smoothed single-subject maps into group contrast maps (z-statistics) and results/ROIs with MNI coordinates are reported (Table 2); voxelwise SPM analyses (with FWE correction) were also performed. Participant sample is appropriate and full article provides methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a delayed-response working memory task (executive function domain: working memory) with emotional and neutral distracters. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects group analysis to identify amygdala sensitivity to emotional > neutral, trial-based voxelwise correlations and across-subject paired t comparisons, conjunction and ANOVA results) and provides coordinates and figures. Within-group contrasts are reported (emotional vs neutral distracters; correct vs incorrect trials), meeting the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Participants are human (healthy young adults). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Stroop task (inhibition/cognitive control), reporting voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses and group-level activation maps. The paper provides within-group task contrasts (conflict-related activity for controls and for unaffected relatives), reports whole-brain results in tables/figures, and describes preprocessing and cluster-thresholding for voxelwise inference. The task falls within executive function/inhibition domain. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes within-group contrasts for multiple participant groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that investigates decision making processes and explicitly links performance to executive functions (DLPFC involvement, attention shifting, working memory, calculation). Methods report voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses with second-level group (random-effects) within-group contrasts (A vs B, A vs C) and cluster-level correction; behavioral and imaging results are provided in full. Participants are a within-group sample (elderly healthy). Reporting includes coordinates/tables/figures. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10; no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines visual working memory (multiple object permanence tracking — MOPT), addressing dynamic updating and feature binding (falls within the working memory executive-function domain). The paper reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects SPM99; significance thresholds and cluster-level correction) and provides coordinates (Table 1) and activation maps. Within-group task contrasts are reported (MT−MC and ST−SC planned subtractions), comparing test and control conditions. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are presented as voxelwise maps and tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, behavioral and fMRI results, ROI analyses, discussion, and references, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical imaging data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical PET task-based study that directly assesses executive-type processes (territorial planning and checkmate judgment) using within-subject, within-group task contrasts. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses (thresholds, group comparisons, and correlation analyses) rather than ROI-only results. Tasks map to established executive domains (planning/strategic decision-making). Group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps are described for professionals and amateurs, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI (simultaneously with ERPs) using an auditory go/nogo paradigm assessing inhibitory control (an executive function). The paper presents voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses (nogo minus control) for within-group contrasts in both alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls, with whole-brain thresholding and cluster reporting. Although imaging coverage appears limited (10 functional slices), the analysis is voxelwise and partial-brain acquisition is allowed by the review criteria. Results are described in the main text (frontal, temporal, parietal activations) meeting reporting requirements. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I7: it does not report a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation map for the emotional Stroop contrast. Although it is an fMRI study of an inhibition/cognitive-control task (emotional Stroop) and contains within-group contrasts (positive vs neutral) and reports ROI-based AC activation and voxelwise PPI (functional connectivity) results, the main task activation results are restricted to an a priori AC ROI rather than a whole-brain voxelwise task activation map required by I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I7.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of analogical reasoning that explicitly manipulates and measures working memory and relational-integration processes. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) and within-group contrasts (e.g., ANA > CAT, ANA > SEM) with tables/figures of activation, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participants are healthy adults and within-group task contrasts are provided. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (set-shifting/planning) using the Montreal Card-Sorting Task. The full text reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level statistical maps (thresholding and cluster extents described) and provides within-group contrasts (e.g., retrieval without shift vs control, retrieval with shift vs retrieval without shift, continuous shift vs control) for both patient and control groups. Results are reported in tables and figures and described in the text. The participant sample (Parkinson’s patients and matched controls) is acceptable per inclusion rule I9. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Hence it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. The study is therefore appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis pooling executive-function task activations.

This study does not assess executive function using a task-based paradigm. While it reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (I7) and includes within-group task contrasts (violent vs fearful/neutral) (I8), involves healthy adult participants (I9), and reports whole-brain results in text/figures (I10), it does not meet I5 or I6: the primary experimental paradigm is passive viewing of film clips (violent/fearful/neutral) rather than tasks within established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). No exclusion criteria are met (exclusion_criteria_applied: []). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on executive-function task activations.

Full text incomplete; only abstract/metadata available. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met (based on abstract): I5 (PET, task-based paradigm assessing brain activation), I8 (within-group contrasts reported: rest vs movement and sequence length effects), I9 (participant group reported; within-group contrasts present). Inclusion IDs not met / cannot confirm due to missing full text: I6 (uncertain whether the finger-sequence task was intended as an executive-function task within established domains — authors suggest involvement of spatial working memory but task may be primarily motor), I7 (cannot confirm that at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical map/analysis is reported), I10 (unable to verify the format of whole-brain results e.g., coordinates/voxelwise maps). Because core methods/results are not available, I cannot verify all required inclusion criteria; therefore exclude pending full-text review.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive control (flanker/ANT) in autism and neurotypical participants. It explicitly assesses executive/inhibitory control (I5,I6) using a task that manipulates congruency and arousal. Analyses report whole-brain, voxelwise procedures (group-averaged t-maps, FDR thresholds, random-effects contrasts) meeting whole-brain evidence requirements (I7). The paper includes within-group task contrasts (incongruent vs congruent and high- vs low-arousal conditions) and reports within-group activation maps and timecourses (I8). Clinical and control groups are included (I9). Whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures (I10). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses, not solely connectivity/resting-state, and within-group activation contrasts are reported. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI, task-based empirical study of hypothesis generation that the authors link to working memory and higher-order inferential processes (meets I5 and I6). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with tables of Talairach coordinates and surface maps (meets I7 and I10). Within-group task contrasts are reported (hypothesis generation vs baseline; and pre- vs post-training within the trained group), satisfying I8. Participants are healthy undergraduates (acceptable per I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study using an executive-function task (two-back working memory) and reports within-group task vs fixation measures, so it meets I5, I6, I8, and I9. However, the paper’s analyses are focused on thalamic ROI-based task activation measures and do not present any group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps in this full text (the authors note whole-brain exploratory analyses were published elsewhere). Therefore it fails I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses reported with no voxelwise results in this article). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study with within-group voxelwise contrasts (MI vs LI) in healthy adults and reports results in-text and figures, the primary task is visual object categorization manipulated by stimulus impoverishment. While the authors interpret activations as reflecting top-down control and implicate working memory and attention, the fMRI task itself does not directly implement or manipulate a canonical executive-function domain listed in the inclusion criteria (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The explicit working-memory manipulation was behavioral (Experiment 2) and not a whole-brain fMRI task contrast. Therefore I6 (task within established executive function domains) is not satisfied, so the study does not meet all inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly assesses verbal working memory and associated executive processes (active search, decision-making, attentional maintenance). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (fixed- and random-effects VT vs baseline contrasts) with peak coordinates and SPM maps. The task falls within the working memory domain of executive function, includes a within-group task contrast, and presents whole-brain results in tables/figures. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is an empirical PET task-based study that explicitly probes spatial working memory and planning during covered maze traversal, which fall within executive function domains (working memory/planning). The study reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., covered vs motor, covered vs visual, covered vs uncovered), with stereotactic coordinates and SPM{Z} maps described in the text. Participants (healthy adults) are a qualifying group and whole-brain results are reported in coordinates/tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based paradigm that manipulates working-memory/task difficulty in a visuospatial paired-associate task (executive function domain: working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM random-effects one-sample and two-sample t-tests), thresholded maps and tables of coordinates, and within-group task contrasts (e.g., RET6 vs RET3, parametric load regressors, zero/first/second-order contrasts). Participant groups are healthy young and older adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are presented in tables, figures and text. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of antisaccades (inhibition), which falls within executive function/inhibition domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM99), thresholded and reported in MNI space, and presents within-group task contrasts (antisaccade vs prosaccade; saccades vs fixation). Participant sample is healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are reported as voxelwise maps and ROI/time-course follow-ups with coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study examining a cognitive control strategy (“reality checking”) during anticipation of emotional stimuli. It meets I5: fMRI study assessing cognitive control. It meets I6: the task requires executive control/inhibition of anticipatory emotional responses (falls within executive function/cognitive control domain). It meets I7: whole-brain voxelwise group-level random-effects analyses are reported (voxelwise contrasts, cluster thresholds). It meets I8: within-group task contrasts are reported (negative vs neutral; unknown vs neutral). It meets I9: participant group (healthy adults) qualifies. It meets I10: whole-brain results are reported in tables and figures described in text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (executive function domain) reporting group-level voxelwise activation contrasts (e.g., HIGH>LOW, ORG>HIGH) with whole-brain GLM analyses and reported activation clusters/figures. It includes within-group task contrasts, healthy participant group data, and whole-brain results presented in tables and figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/task switching in healthy adults. It reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (e.g., shift vs repeat; high vs low response and stimulus conflict), provides statistical thresholds and cluster criteria, and presents group-level activation results in the main text and supplemental materials. The task (task switching; cognitive flexibility) falls squarely within executive function domains. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or between-group contrasts, and the paper is an empirical report with original human neuroimaging data. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) using an event-related parametric paradigm. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise second-level analyses (e.g., L1>Control, L2>L1, L3>L2) with voxel-level thresholds and cluster correction, whole-brain normalization and coordinates in tables and figures. Results include group-level statistical maps and Talairach/MNI coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and References, so the full text appears complete.

Although this PET study used task-based paradigms (FDG with an auditory continuous performance task — vigilance) and includes clinical groups (meeting I5, I6, I9), it does not report any group-level, voxelwise within-group task-activation statistical maps. Analyses are based on absolute regional values sampled from 34 predefined ROIs and correlation comparisons across groups (ROI-based/regional coupling). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group maps) and I8 (within-group task contrast). This also violates exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise results) and E5 (no within-group task activation contrast reported). Full text appears complete. Excluded for not providing the required voxelwise within-group activation maps needed for the meta-analysis of task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group SDM and t-statistic maps), within-group task vs control contrasts, and presents maps and a table of local maxima. Participants are a within-group sample of 20 healthy adults. These satisfy inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables and references).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task-based arithmetic verification paradigm that probes cognitive control/working memory and interference resolution (executive functions). The study reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM99) contrasting incorrect vs. correct equations (a within-group task contrast), with whole-brain coverage and results presented as significant clusters/figures/tables. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy subjects. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with voxelwise whole-brain analyses and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (verbal fluency) reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (generation > repetition for easy and hard letters), provides voxelwise statistical maps and corrected results (FDR) and coordinates, and includes both healthy and clinical (schizophrenia) participant groups. The full article contains background, methods, results, and discussion (supplementary material noted but not required). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based PET study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps (SPM) and within-group contrasts (e.g., M_SEQ vs M_PRED, M_ROT vs M_PRED, M_PRED vs S). The M_SEQ task explicitly places heavy demands on spatial working memory and attentional/selection processes (an established executive function domain), and authors report DLPFC and anterior cingulate activations consistent with executive processing. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are presented in detail in the full text (methods, voxelwise analyses, coordinates, and plots). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports a task-based verbal fluency activation paradigm and voxelwise SPM96 analyses (within-group activation for controls and group×condition effects), satisfying inclusion criteria I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, it does not meet I5: the activation imaging was performed with 99mTc-HMPAO SPECT (and the PET data reported were not used for the task activation contrasts). I5 requires fMRI or PET task-based activation; SPECT does not fulfill this modality requirement. Full text appears complete with methods, results and discussion confirming the modality and analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criteria: none applicable (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study that evaluates cognitive control demands of complex mental multiplication, which explicitly involves working memory, strategy planning, and executive demands. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses using SPM (one-sample t-tests; voxelwise p<0.001; cluster extent thresholds) and presents within-group task contrasts (e.g., untrained vs trained, trained vs untrained, and task vs number-matching control). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as tables/figures and described in text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based spatial working memory (spatial span) paradigm, which falls within executive function domains (working memory). The PET experiment reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM99 analyses and voxelwise contrasts (structured vs control; non-structured vs control) with peak coordinates and corrected thresholds, satisfying the requirement for group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps and within-group contrasts. Participants include healthy volunteers (PET) and patient groups (behavioural), so any participant group criterion is met. Whole-brain results are reported with coordinates and ROI analyses in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical neuroimaging data are reported). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study that probes voluntary inhibition of the micturition reflex via an experimental pelvic-floor contraction paradigm (full vs empty bladder) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation maps (with coordinates and cluster statistics). The task targets inhibition (an established executive-function domain), includes within-group contrasts (FBC > EBC), reports voxelwise group analyses and coordinates, and uses healthy participants. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study directly addressing cognitive control/executive function (temporal integration, sustained maintenance, strategy representation). It uses whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses (state/item mixed design) with group-level random-effects tests and reports clusters/coordinates; within-group task contrasts are reported (task vs fixation; W2 vs W12; WIN×DYN interactions). Participants are healthy adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used FDG-PET acquired during mental rest and analyzed pre/post treatment metabolic changes, not a task-based, task-evoked activation paradigm. Exclusion criterion E4 applies because it reports resting-state (or task-free metabolic) analyses without a task activation map. It does not meet key inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI/PET), I6 (task falls within executive-function task paradigm), I7 (voxelwise task-evoked group map), or I8 (within-group task contrast). It does meet I9 (participant group acceptable) and I10 (reports whole-brain coordinates). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded from a meta-analysis of task-evoked executive-function activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that probes nonspatial attention shifting—a form of cognitive flexibility (executive function). It reports voxelwise, group-level contrasts (e.g., shifting attention vs sustained attention) with stereotactic normalization and reproducible activation foci (tables of coordinates and reproducibility maps). Within-group task contrasts are presented (shifting vs sustained; sustained vs fixation). Participants are healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that probes decision-making under uncertainty and explicitly examines working-memory and related executive processes. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (z-maps, thresholded and reported with Talairach coordinates and tables/figures) including within-group contrasts (uncertain prediction conditions vs control; parametric uncertainty regressors). Tasks fall within the executive domain (working memory/mnemonic search) and participants are a healthy adult group. Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented in tables and figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; thus full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an established executive function). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (including a main effect of task: 2-back vs 0-back) and task×drug and task×group interactions; results are presented as group-level activation maps and tables (with small-volume correction applied but within a voxelwise framework). Thus it provides whole-brain, task-evoked, within-group contrasts. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the document appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study investigating inhibition of return (an inhibitory attentional effect). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects ANOVA; cluster-level correction) with standard within-group task contrasts (e.g., Long_SOA (Cued+Uncued) > Short_SOA; cued vs uncued), and provides coordinates/tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets I5–I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (surface- and volume-based t tests, Fourier analysis) and presents whole-brain/whole-head coverage for group analyses (n=12 for whole-head), with task-versus-passive and identity-vs-location within-group contrasts and group maps/figures/tables. Results include voxelwise statistical maps and ROI and group-average analyses, satisfying requirements for within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise maps.
