No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and include within-group contrasts and original empirical data. Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive inhibition in healthy adults that reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts. The study used SPM99 for voxelwise analysis and reports activations for backward (inhibition) versus motor control and backward versus forward contrasts, with activations described across the whole brain (frontal, parietal, temporal regions). Although slice coverage was limited (16 non-contiguous planes), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted, which satisfies partial-brain acquisition allowance. The manuscript contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is an event-related fMRI study of verbal working memory (Sternberg task) in healthy adults that reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise analyses. The paper provides within-group task contrasts (phase-specific encoding/maintenance/retrieval regressors and high vs low load contrasts), uses conjunctions to identify phase-and-load-sensitive voxels, and presents whole-brain/partial-brain voxelwise maps and coordinate tables/figures. These satisfy inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise group analyses; partial coverage allowed), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (within-group healthy adult sample), and I10 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports group-level, voxelwise activation maps and within-group contrasts relevant to executive function. The working memory (W) task clearly falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports whole-brain acquisition and group statistical parametric maps (SPM t/Z maps) with voxelwise thresholding and presents within-group contrasts (W–C, T–C, T–W). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based gambling/guessing paradigm that the authors explicitly link to working memory and decision-making (executive functions). They acquired whole-brain echo-planar BOLD data (48 axial slices covering the whole brain), conducted voxelwise group-level SPM analyses, and report within-group task contrasts (guessing vs reporting) with activation foci and tables/figures. Participants are healthy volunteers. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for a task activation meta-analysis of executive function and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study of executive function (dual-task and integration) using task-based paradigms. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) including both fixed- and random-effects contrasts (e.g., dual − [auditory + visual], integration − [auditory + visual]) with stereotactic coordinates reported. Within-group task contrasts are presented, results are voxelwise and whole-brain (with small-volume corrections only for a priori regions where specified), and healthy participant data are used. Results are reported as coordinates and statistical maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a Stroop paradigm (cognitive control/inhibition) in healthy participants. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (e.g., IC vs CC contrasts), including tables/coordinates and ROI follow-ups, and presents within-group task contrasts (incongruent vs congruent and emotional word contrasts). These meet the meta-analysis requirements for executive-function task activations and do not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment of methods and contrasts.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive control processes (conflict detection, selection, and suppression) during selective retrieval practice, directly addressing executive-function-related control and inhibition. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level task contrasts (e.g., successful vs. unsuccessful retrieval; first vs. third retrieval), provides coordinate-based results, and includes within-group analyses in a healthy adult sample. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain voxelwise results are reported; not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (GO/NOGO), meeting executive-function domain criteria (inhibition). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, voxelwise thresholding with cluster-correction), and presents within-group task contrasts (event-related Stops vs baseline and Fast vs Slow conditions). Participants are healthy adults; results are reported in figures and tables with cluster coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control (task switching/cognitive flexibility). It reports group-level, voxelwise task contrasts (Stage 3 vs Stage 1 and other within-group contrasts) using whole-brain acquisition and random-effects analyses, with tables/figures of coordinates and ROI and whole-brain results. Participants are neurologically normal adults and within-group contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back paradigm) in schizophrenia and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM99) and explicitly presents within-group contrasts (2-back > 0-back, 2-back degraded > 0-back degraded) for patients and controls; results are reported with coordinates and thresholding details. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory = executive domain), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (clinical participant groups acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, and is empirical. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (Stroop interference; inhibitory control) with healthy developmental participants. The paper includes within-group contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and reports voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain (voxel-wise) analyses and maps/tables of age and performance correlations (voxel-wise regression with cluster thresholding). Although slice coverage was partial (only 6 slices used for all subjects), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-only. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study examining working memory (an executive function domain) in schizophrenia and healthy controls. Methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise SPM5 analyses (one-sample t-tests within groups, repeated-measures ANOVA, voxelwise group comparisons) and report coordinate results and cluster statistics. Within-group contrasts (exponential signal decreases across retrieval blocks; main effect of task vs baseline) are explicitly reported for both patients and controls. Participants and task meet inclusion criteria, and reporting of whole-brain voxelwise results in text/tables satisfies reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of mental rotation/visuo-spatial working memory (an executive function domain: working memory). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses using SPM2, including within-group task contrasts (mental rotation vs passive viewing; one-sample and paired t-tests). Results are presented as coordinates, tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults (women tested in two cycle phases, men once). The paper therefore satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains within-group activation contrasts).

This is a task-based, empirical fMRI study (with simultaneous ERP validation) using a visual three-stimulus oddball paradigm that probes attention, working memory encoding, and vigilance—domains of executive function. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM maps and contrasts (target vs. standard; distractor vs. standard) with corrected statistical maps and tables/figures of activations. Thus it provides within-group task contrasts and voxelwise whole-brain results. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only analyses; the study is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) that reports group-level, voxelwise SPM contrasts (e.g., REP/REP CONT, MAT/MAT CONT, REP/MAT) with thresholded whole-brain maps and tables/figures. Although lower temporal/occipital lobes and cerebellum were not imaged (partial-brain coverage), the analyses are voxelwise and meet the meta-analysis’ allowance for partial coverage. Within-group task contrasts are reported and described in detail. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (only ROIs, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are triggered. Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive control (dual-task and task-switching), reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (SPM96 fixed-effects) with stereotactic coordinates (Table 1). Within-group contrasts are reported (dual-task vs baseline, task-switching vs baseline, dual vs switch, switch vs dual). Participants are healthy adults. Results are presented as voxelwise statistical maps and coordinate tables in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and figures/tables. Therefore it meets I5–I10 and qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study appears to report resting-state fMRI connectivity/ resting networks in MCI and mild AD rather than a task-based executive function activation paradigm. Exclusion IDs met: E4 (resting-state/connectivity analyses without task activation maps). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function), I6 (no executive function task domain reported), I7 (no whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation map reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text is not available here (only title/metadata/redirect notice), so I set fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is moderate. If full text confirms a task-based analysis, decision should be revisited.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study examining working-memory manipulation (an executive function domain) during numerical, verbal, and spatial tasks. It satisfies inclusion criteria: I5 (fMRI task-based study of executive/cognitive control processes), I6 (tasks are working memory manipulation, an established executive domain), I7 (voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses reported using SPM with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported, e.g., Manipulation minus Maintenance for each material), I9 (within-group data from healthy adult participants), and I10 (whole-brain results presented in text, tables, and figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study that reports voxelwise group-level task activations for working memory tasks involving facial affect. It uses task vs rest contrasts within each group (mnemonic and anticipatory WM conditions) analyzed with SPM99 and reports whole-brain (though partial-volume) voxelwise results in figures and a table of Talairach coordinates. Tasks fall squarely within the executive function domain (working memory). Both patient and control groups have within-group activation maps reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI task study using a covert orienting paradigm probing inhibition of return (an inhibitory attentional process). It reports within-subject, within-group voxelwise contrasts (long SOA vs short SOA) using SPM random-effects whole-brain analyses with coordinates and cluster statistics, and presents behavioral and imaging results for healthy participants and drug conditions. These features satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for task-based executive/inhibitory control activations, whole-brain voxelwise group maps, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly assesses spatial attention and short-term visuospatial memory (working memory), an established executive function domain. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (task − control contrasts for SAMP and MPP), with whole-brain coverage (except posterior cerebellum) and thresholded cluster results and coordinates in tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults and results are presented as whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a Stroop paradigm (inhibition/conflict-monitoring), clearly within executive-function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses with whole-brain coverage and provides activation coordinates and corrected thresholds (FDR), and presents within-group task contrasts (conflict/incongruent vs congruent; conflict-level contrasts) and group-level task activation maps. EEG connectivity is additional but does not replace task activation reporting. Thus it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group contrasts are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of episodic associative memory encoding (face–name–city triplets). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., hit discontinuous vs hit simultaneous; associative formation vs misses) and thus meets I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the study’s primary aim and task probe episodic memory/associative encoding, not an established executive-function paradigm. Although the authors discuss working-memory and executive contributions, the task was not designed or analysed as a working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation task. Therefore it does not meet I5 and I6 (does not primarily assess executive function/cognitive control within established EF domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study that tests phonological control and verbal working memory during a syllable-judgment task (task-based executive function within the working memory domain). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (e.g., All Trials>Fixation; contrasts across word types) with coordinates and figures, and includes within-group task contrasts against fixation and between task conditions. Participant group is healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study reporting within-group voxelwise task contrasts and coordinates, the task's primary domain is discourse comprehension and pragmatic inferencing rather than an established executive function domain. The study does report engagement of executive-control regions, but the paradigm was designed to probe text coherence/inference processes (language comprehension) and not canonical executive function tasks (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet the requirement that tasks fall within established executive function domains (I6) and arguably does not primarily assess executive function/cognitive control per I5. Whole-text is complete.

This is an empirical PET study with task-based contrasts probing working memory (1-back, 2-back, random-number generation), which falls under executive function. Group-level, voxelwise analyses using SPM99 and multivariate PLS are reported, with within-group task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs reading) and reported activations/coordinates. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are whole-brain voxelwise and described in text/contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study of task-switching and endogenous control (executive function: cognitive flexibility/working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects contrasts (e.g., transition cue vs task cue) with Z-maps, cluster thresholds, and tables of coordinates; within-group task contrasts and main effects are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task study with full methods, within-group voxelwise contrasts and whole-brain random-effects analysis (meets I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the task is a smooth-pursuit oculomotor paradigm investigating visuomotor/predictive and attentional mechanisms rather than an executive function or cognitive-control task as defined by the review (does NOT meet I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no E3–E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails the required inclusion criteria I5 and I6 (not an executive-function task). Inclusion IDs met: I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion IDs not met: I5, I6. Exclusion IDs met: none ([]).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of working memory (a core executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses (whole-brain), presents within-group task contrasts (WM delay/encoding/retrieval vs baseline and condition contrasts novel vs familiar), and reports coordinates and time courses. Participants are healthy volunteer groups with within-group contrasts reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a three-back working memory task with high-interference (lure) trials assessing attentional control/executive function. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (voxelwise thresholds, cluster criteria, atlas-space normalization) and within-group task effects (event-related and sustained task activity versus fixation baseline and trial-type contrasts). Results are reported across the whole brain and as coordinates/region tables. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task domain (working memory/executive control), modality (fMRI), whole-brain voxelwise reporting, and within-group task contrasts; no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using the color–word Stroop (a well-established inhibitory/cognitive control executive function task). It reports within-group, event-related contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent; congruent+incongruent > neutral) analyzed with group random-effects voxelwise statistics (thresholding and cluster extent reported). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and results are described in text, figures, and tables. Although acquisition used limited slices (13 contiguous slices), the inclusion criteria explicitly allow partial-brain acquisitions provided analyses are voxelwise, which is satisfied here. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so core article content is present.

This is an empirical PET study using task-based working memory paradigms (3-item static and 2-back dynamic), which are established executive-function tasks. The paper reports within-group task contrasts and group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain SPM maps and figures), as well as quantitative ROI results; thus whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps and within-group contrasts are present for participant groups (hypertensives and controls). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a Go/NoGo inhibition task (executive function: inhibition). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and multiple within-group task contrasts (false alarms–hits; correct rejections–hits; false alarms–correct rejections). Results are presented as voxelwise contrasts and interrogated with small-volume corrections but whole-brain voxelwise analyses are explicitly described, satisfying reporting via tables/figures/text. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (antisaccade task) reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts. The sample (children, adolescents, adults) is acceptable. The paper provides full methods, voxelwise statistical maps and time-course analyses (main effects of task and response-type contrasts vs. baseline), fulfilling the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study reports task-based activation for executive function (working memory 1-back task) in both AD patients and healthy elderly, including within-group task contrasts and before/after treatment comparisons. Imaging analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise SPM2 group-level analyses with reported activation clusters (coordinates/figures described). Results include within-group main effects of task and direct within-subject contrasts. Participant groups (clinical AD and elderly controls) are acceptable. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion).

This is an original, task-based fMRI study examining contextual inhibition (an executive function: inhibition). The paper reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain analyses (ACT vs REST, INH vs REST, conjunctions) with corrected statistical maps and tables/figures, and provides group-level results. Participants are healthy adults and contrasts are within-group. Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables of coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function activation meta-analysis.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on the abstract, the study is an event-related BOLD fMRI task-switching investigation addressing attentional control (meets I5 and I6) and reports condition comparisons consistent with within-group task contrasts (meets I8). However, the available content does not allow verification of critical inclusion criterion I7 (that at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analysis/map is reported); it is unclear whether results are from whole-brain voxelwise analyses versus ROI-only analyses, and I10 (format/location of whole-brain results) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the abstract alone, but because not all required inclusion criteria can be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending full-text availability.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of the Stroop task (inhibition/cognitive control), reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper provides full methods, participants (n=14), task details, and within-group contrasts (SI vs CO; RI vs SI) with voxelwise thresholding and coordinate reporting. Results and discussion present whole-brain activations and figures/tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, empirical data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of feedback/decision-making that probes working memory, uncertainty management, conflict monitoring and strategy learning—domains of executive function. The full text reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM2) including one-sample t-tests and repeated-measures ANOVAs, with tables of MNI coordinates and phase and feedback within-group contrasts (exploratory vs. proficiency; gain vs. loss; correct vs. wrong). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (right-handed females). Thus the paper provides voxelwise, within-group task activation maps and coordinate reporting suitable for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (unusual > canonical, canonical > unusual) and provides coordinates and figures, but the tasks are visual object categorization and recognition (with mental rotation and object-sensitive localizers). These tasks probe vision, object memory, and spatial transformation processes rather than established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although working memory and cognitive-control processes are discussed and localizers/secondary tasks are used, the primary experimental contrasts do not constitute core executive function tasks as defined by the review. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (within-group contrasts reported in healthy participants), I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based PET study (H2¹5O) of executive function (random number generation) with clinical (Parkinson's disease) and control groups. It reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (RNG vs COUNT) using SPM96 and provides whole-brain results with coordinates, statistical maps, and tables. Analyses include group-level voxelwise contrasts, rate manipulations (parametric), and detailed localization (Talairach/Brodmann coordinates). All inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables described).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a delayed face recognition (working memory) task, which falls within executive function domains (working memory). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise statistical contrasts (match vs nonmatch) and a whole-brain random-effects analysis with Talairach-normalized t maps (voxelwise thresholding), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are reported in both ROI and whole-brain maps/coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a delayed match-to-sample working memory task (executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM2 one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs), whole-brain thresholding and tables/figures, and within-group task contrasts (e.g., DMS delay > CON delay; object vs. location; familiar vs. trial-unique). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly tests cognitive control/conflict and response inhibition during intentional false responding. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 random-effects, FDR-corrected maps) and provides coordinate tables and figures for within-group contrasts (e.g., FALSE > TRUE, AUTO > NONAUTO). Healthy adult participants were tested and multiple within-group task contrasts are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (abstract reasoning and a match-to-sample working memory task) with healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (contrasts: R>Rc, M>Mc, R>M, M>R) with FDR-corrected statistical maps and peak coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Reporting includes anatomically defined ROIs and whole-brain SPM results (tables/figures with coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and is suitable for inclusion.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that investigates antisaccade (inhibition) and visually guided saccade performance. It falls squarely within the executive function domain of inhibition. The methods report voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM99), present statistical parametric maps and tables of coordinates for group-level within-group contrasts (saccade vs control; antisaccade vs control; antisaccade vs saccade). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy volunteers. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references, and appears complete.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of task switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility). The full text reports methods, voxelwise whole-brain GLM group-level contrasts (one-sample t-tests/random effects), within-group task contrasts (switch vs repeat; main effects and interactions), and tables/figures describing results. Partial-slice coverage is acceptable (they report slice parameters and whole-brain coverage), and results are reported in tables/figures in the text. The article therefore meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive-function activation mapping and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study employing a picture-word (Stroop-like) paradigm that probes semantic interference and the resolution of distractor-related competition via attention/inhibitory control. The task therefore indexes cognitive control/inhibition (an executive function domain). The paper reports a within-group voxelwise contrast (semantically-related distractor vs lexical control) analyzed with SPM99, whole-brain correction and volume-of-interest corrections, and reports coordinates of differential activations (Table II, figures). Participants are healthy adults. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control), I6 (inhibition/attentional control domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with reported coordinates), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a Go/NoGo response-inhibition paradigm (executive function: inhibition). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (one-sample t test) of the within-group contrast Go/NoGo versus Go and provides whole-brain results (tables, coordinates, figures) as well as between-group comparisons. Participant sample (healthy adult males) is acceptable. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) that reports group-level, voxelwise activation analyses (SPM fixed- and random-effects) with coordinates in tables/figures. The paper includes within-group task contrasts (activation vs rest for mnemonic and anticipatory working-memory conditions) for both control and schizophrenia groups. Although slice coverage was partial, I7 allows partial-brain acquisition provided voxelwise analyses are reported. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for task type, domain, voxelwise whole-brain analysis, within-group contrasts, and reporting format.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that probes emotional conflict resolution — a form of cognitive control/inhibition — using a modified Stroop paradigm. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM random-effects contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs congruent; high vs low conflict-resolution), whole-brain/search-volume analyses, and within-group task contrasts in healthy volunteers. It therefore meets all inclusion criteria for an executive-function activation meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study that investigates pro- and anti-saccade tasks, which probe inhibitory control (anti-saccade requires suppression of a prepotent response) — an established executive function domain (inhibition). The paper reports task-based, voxelwise analyses identifying activated voxels (t-test corrected for multiple comparisons) and provides Talairach coordinates for activations. Within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., pro-saccade vs fixation localizer; anti- vs pro-saccade comparisons; task vs baseline), and statistical analyses are conducted across subjects. Although imaging used partial slice coverage (focused on frontal and parietal cortex), the meta-analysis inclusion criterion allows partial-brain acquisition provided voxelwise analyses are reported. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a delayed-response working memory task with emotional and neutral distracters (task-based paradigm assessing executive function: working memory). The Methods report voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses and contrasts (e.g., emotional vs neutral, emotional vs scrambled) with coordinates and thresholding, satisfying within-group task contrasts. Participants are a defined healthy adult group. Whole-brain results are reported in figures and tables. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, nor is it non-empirical). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables referenced) is provided and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the color–word Stroop task (an inhibition/cognitive control/executive function paradigm) with within-group Stroop vs baseline contrasts. Group-level voxelwise statistical maps and Talairach-coordinate tables are reported; although slice coverage was limited, analyses were voxelwise and group-averaged label- and activation-maps are presented. Results include coordinates and figures of whole-brain (partial coverage) activation maps. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a visual three-stimulus oddball task assessing selective/sustained attention (vigilance), which falls within the executive domain of vigilance. The full text reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (one-sample random-effects t-tests for targets, distractors, standards) and presents whole-brain, voxelwise statistical maps and clusterwise-corrected results (figures and tables). Analyses include both fixed- and random-effects group-level voxelwise maps (voxelwise thresholds and clusterwise correction), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participants are a defined human sample (older postmenopausal women). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is an empirical neuroimaging paper). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes a voluntary blink-inhibition condition (subjects instructed to inhibit blinking) and models spontaneous blink events. Analyses include within-group voxelwise contrasts (blink inhibition vs closed-eye baseline; event-related analyses of spontaneous blinks) using SPM99 with group-level random-effects and whole-brain thresholds reported (cluster-corrected p<0.05; activations listed in tables/figures). The task falls within the executive-function domain of inhibition (voluntary suppression of a prepotent/motor response). Participants are healthy adults and at least one within-group task contrast is reported. Whole-brain voxelwise results are provided and described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly investigates response inhibition, an executive function (inhibition). Methods report whole-brain acquisition (contiguous slices covering entire brain) and voxelwise group analyses (one-sample t tests across 14 subjects) time-locked to lure (No-Go) events, constituting a within-group task contrast. Results are reported with cluster maps, figures, and Talairach coordinates (Table 1 and figures). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Paced Visual Serial Addition Task (PVSAT), which targets working memory/executive processes. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain group-level analyses (SPM2) including within-group contrasts (calculation vs control) for controls, CIS, and CDMS groups, with thresholds and cluster correction described. Results are reported in the text, tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an original event-related fMRI study (re-analysis of five datasets) that assesses motor response inhibition (Go/NoGo), an executive function domain (inhibition). The manuscript reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (voxelwise t-tests, cluster thresholds, Talairach normalization) and presents within-group task contrasts (STOPS vs baseline/ongoing Go trials) and split-group contrasts; results are reported as activation maps and ROI analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods (task, scanning, preprocessing, voxelwise analysis), results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical or only between-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task-evoked executive-function activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that tests neural recruitment for quantifier comprehension and explicitly examines involvement of executive resources (working memory) in higher-order quantifiers. It used whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM99, random-effects t-tests) with full-brain coverage and reports peak coordinates and figures/tables. Within-group task contrasts are reported (proposition+response minus proposition alone; higher-order vs first-order), and behavioral performance is provided. Participants are healthy adults. Results include whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study of executive control processes (semantic retrieval, monitoring, working memory). It uses group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., SemSp – SylSp; SemVoCo – SemSp) reported with peak coordinates and figures. Tasks target working memory/controlled semantic processing (an executive domain). Results include whole-brain corrected statistical maps and coordinate reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data present). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise activation contrasts for reasoning tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task-based study assessing cognitive control/executive processes — reasoning tasks engage executive processes), I6 (tasks involve maintenance and manipulation of information consistent with the working memory/executive domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses with group-level reporting of activated ROIs and Talairach coordinates), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported: conditional vs baseline, relational vs baseline, conditional vs relational), I9 (healthy adult participant group; within-group contrasts reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates and Z-scores in text/tables/figures). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

The study is an fMRI task-based investigation and reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (test vs control) with whole-brain results (p<0.001 FWE), satisfying I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the experimental task is the Word Memory Test (delayed recognition), an episodic verbal memory/symptom validity task rather than a canonical executive function or cognitive-control task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet I5 (study assessing executive function or cognitive control) nor I6 (task falls within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of reasoning/problem solving that probes relational complexity and executive processes (working memory/integration/planning). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99 linear-trend and subtraction contrasts), with within-group task contrasts (task vs rest; complexity and distractor contrasts; complexity-level linear trends) and tables/figures of activations. Participants are healthy adults (right-handed college students). Results include coordinates and rendered maps. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This fMRI study reports task-evoked whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses for cognitive tasks relevant to executive function. The Paced Auditory Serial Addition Test (PASAT) probes sustained attention, information processing speed, and working memory (an established executive domain); the study also included a recall (memory retrieval) task. The paper reports within-group one-sample SPM99 contrasts for patients and controls, between-group two-sample contrasts, multiple regression correlations with lesion load, and tables/figures of coordinate results — satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group task contrasts). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical PET study using task-based activation (H2(15)O PET) that directly tests an executive function (counting Stroop — cognitive control/inhibition). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level SPM99 analyses contrasting incongruent vs. neutral conditions (a within-group task contrast), and it includes both whole-brain analyses and ROI/small-volume-corrected results with coordinates and tables reported. Participants are a defined group of healthy volunteers. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based PET study reporting within-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing non-stereotyped (recognition, response reversal, random pairing) vs stereotyped retrieval. Tasks include cognitive flexibility/set-shifting (response reversal, random pairing) which fall within executive function domains. Analyses used SPM voxelwise group contrasts with reported coordinates and regional results. Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (Rotation>Control; Intact>Scrambled; Saccade>Fixation). The mental rotation task engages visuospatial transformation and working memory/cognitive control processes, which fall within executive function domains (working memory/cognitive control). Whole-brain SPMs and coordinate tables are reported, and within-group voxelwise contrasts are presented. Participants are a within-group healthy sample. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive control/interference resolution (recent-probes working memory and verb-generation selection). Group-level, voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses are reported (including whole-brain and ROI results) with coordinates and within-group contrasts (recent vs non-recent; many vs few). Participants are healthy adults and the full article (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a task that probes selective attention and spatial negative priming (inhibition). It meets inclusion: (I5) fMRI task-based study; (I6) addresses inhibition, an established executive function domain; (I7) reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-versus-rest statistical maps (P<0.05 corrected); (I8) includes within-group contrasts (task vs rest and condition comparisons within the same participant group); (I9) reports a within-group analysis in healthy adult participants; (I10) provides whole-brain results in figures and tables/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the counting Stroop (inhibition/cognitive control) that reports voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (AFNI, Talairach normalization, cluster-thresholding) and a within-group contrast (incongruent vs. congruent). Healthy adult participants were tested and results are reported in text/tables/figures (including coordinates and cluster results). The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study (MSIT) probing cognitive control/interference in healthy adults. The paper reports within-group voxelwise interference vs control contrasts at both individual and group levels, including group-averaged voxelwise t-tests in Talairach space and tables/figures of whole-brain activations. The task falls squarely within executive function/inhibition and cognitive control domains, and results include behavioral (RT, errors) and imaging maps. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain) using an event-related Sternberg paradigm in premanifest Huntington’s disease and matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM5) including within-group one-sample t-tests for ICA-derived task-related components and provides stereotaxic coordinates and statistical thresholds. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts/maps), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/results clearly described). The study is empirical, not ROI-only, and not limited to connectivity-only analyses (it reports task-evoked spatial ICA components and voxelwise maps), so no exclusion criteria apply (E3–E6 not met). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical PET study with task-based manipulations that explicitly examine attentional/control (executive) processes in interaction with learning/memory. It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (thresholding, Talairach coordinates) and multiple within-group contrasts (NR-RS, TR-RS, NR-TR, interaction contrasts). The tasks engage executive components such as working memory/visuo-spatial sketchpad, initiation, monitoring, response selection, and top-down attentional control (PFC, ACC, PPC activations discussed), mapping onto the review’s executive domains (notably working memory and initiation/planning/monitoring). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and within-group contrasts are present. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an empirical task-based fMRI study using the PASAT (a working-memory/executive function task) in patients (CISSMS) and matched healthy controls. Methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects group analyses (SPM99), with within-group one-sample t-tests (task vs control) and between-group contrasts; results include regional activations and correlations. Although EPI acquisition used 17 slices (partial coverage), analyses were voxelwise and therefore satisfy the meta-analysis allowance for partial-brain studies. The study provides within-group task contrasts for at least one group (controls and patients) and reports whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/results in text/figures/tables. All inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts. The mental arithmetic tasks explicitly engage working memory and executive control; the paper interprets findings in terms of working memory and executive processes and reports within-group contrasts (untrained vs trained multiplication/subtraction). Whole-brain SPM2 random-effects analyses and tables/figures of voxelwise results are provided. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the submission. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study).

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines visual working memory (VSTM) and perceptual attention tasks (delayed match-to-sample VSTM and related perceptual controls). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM, FDR-corrected maps) and presents coordinates/tables and within-group task contrasts (K-weighted and set-size regressors). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations (working memory domain). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that examines decision-making/feedback processing and prefrontal/striatal responses in PTSD. The task engages executive processes (learning, working memory, hypothesis testing, and set-shifting) consistent with established executive-function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level SPM analyses (ANOVAs) with tables/coordinates and figures, and presents within-group contrasts (gains vs losses) for patients and controls as well as phase comparisons. Participants include a clinical PTSD group (allowed). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study includes group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (visual search vs control; memory search vs control), reports whole-brain coordinates, and tests healthy adults, so it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the tasks are visual search and long-term memory search (attention/episodic retrieval), not clearly within the meta-analysis’ required executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although authors discuss monitoring/manipulation and possible planning, the paradigms are primarily attention and memory-search tasks rather than established executive-function tasks, so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting inclusion criterion I6.

This is an empirical H2 15 O PET study using a task-based Stroop paradigm (inhibition/cognitive control), satisfying executive-function domain requirements. The paper reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain analyses (NPAIRS/CV canonical eigenimages with voxelwise thresholds P<0.001 and cluster extent) and explicitly describes within-group task contrasts (congruent vs incongruent Stroop conditions) with behavioral correlations. Participant groups (first-episode antipsychotic-naïve patients and controls) are appropriate and at least one group reports within-group task activation maps. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI or connectivity/resting analyses, and it includes within-group activation contrasts (so E3–E5 do not apply) and is empirical (not E6). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a modified Stroop task (an inhibition/selective-attention executive function paradigm). The paper reports within-group voxelwise activation maps (SPM99) for both patients and controls (Stroop activation vs rest), includes group-level random-effects comparisons, and provides whole-brain results in tables and figures. Although slice coverage was limited (15 slices), analyses were voxelwise and reported comprehensively. All required inclusion criteria for task, modality, within-group contrasts, and whole-brain voxelwise reporting are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of antisaccade performance (response inhibition/volitional control), which falls within executive-function domains (inhibition). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM2 (standard antisaccade vs fixation and delayed-task contrasts), with coordinates, tables, and figures provided. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (standard antisaccade > fixation; SaccadeTask and DelayCondition ANOVAs), satisfying the requirement for task-evoked maps. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and references; core content is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not only between-group contrasts; not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and should be included.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used task-based fMRI (modified PASAT) targeting executive/working-memory processes (I5,I6), reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps analyzed in SPM2 with FDR correction and figures/tables (I7,I10), and presents within-group task contrasts for the combined sample and separately for CFS and control groups (I8,I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that probes language control using trial-by-trial cued naming and language/task switching—paradigms that place demands on executive processes (cognitive flexibility and inhibition). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise random-effects analyses (second-level SPM), with multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., LSc vs SNc, LSc vs TSc, L2 vs L1) and tables/figures of activations. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text is present (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (delayed recognition of locations), which falls within executive function domains (working memory). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (delay-period activity vs baseline) and presents group-level voxelwise analyses (spatial normalization-based group analysis with group maps and voxelwise thresholding), satisfying the whole-brain, voxelwise requirement. Participant sample and methods are described. Whole-brain results are reported in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text is provided (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and violates none.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using task-based paradigms that probe categorization with a delayed match-to-sample (DMS) design that requires stimulus maintenance and comparison. The tasks implicate working memory/executive processing (authors explicitly interpret categorization as involving working memory), and the manuscript reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (CAT vs AUD, CAT vs Rest, AUD vs Rest) using SPM random-effects group analyses, figures, and tables of MNI/Talairach coordinates. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (random-effects, cluster thresholds) despite limited slice coverage (22 slices); partial-brain acquisition is allowable per inclusion rules. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported as group-level activation maps and coordinate tables. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation contrasts for within-group task comparisons. Although the primary focus is implicit sequence learning, the authors explicitly interpret activations in terms of spatial working memory and response monitoring (executive/cognitive control processes). The study used voxelwise SPM analyses with cluster-level correction across the entire brain, and contrasts compare fixed-sequence vs random-order blocks (within-group). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported in figures and tables. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory/selective attention (executive function domain) that reports group-level, voxelwise univariate activation contrasts and whole-brain functional connectivity analyses. The paper includes within-group task contrasts (Remember/Ignore vs Passive View) analyzed at the group random-effects level with voxelwise thresholds and reports maps/tables of results. Participant sample and task design are described. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function fMRI studies and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 random-effects, coordinates and activation maps) and within-group contrasts (R>NR, A>NA, main effects), using healthy adult participants. The tasks engage executive processes (verbal working memory, response selection/conflict detection/monitoring, initiation/search strategy) as described by the authors, placing them within established executive-function domains. Results are reported as coordinates, tables and figures. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study with group-level voxelwise maps and within-group contrasts, but the tasks (lexicosemantic decision, tone discrimination, and visuomotor sequence learning) do not target established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails the core inclusion criteria I5 and I6 required for a meta-analysis of executive function activations. It does meet criteria for whole-brain voxelwise analysis and within-group contrasts, and participant sampling is acceptable, but the cognitive domains assessed are outside the review scope.

Although this is a PET study with executive-like tasks (Divided Attention, Flexibility) and reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results and stereotactic coordinates, the imaging was not task-evoked. 18-FDG uptake was measured while subjects relaxed with eyes closed (to capture tonic pharmacological effects) and neuropsychological testing was performed outside the 18-FDG uptake period. The reported voxelwise contrasts are pharmacological condition contrasts (ethanol influx/elimination vs placebo) and correlations between test performance and metabolism, not within-group task-versus-baseline activation maps. Therefore the study does NOT meet key inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function during imaging), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), and I8 (within-group task contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (tasks fall within executive domains), I9 (acceptable participant group), I10 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Excluded on the basis of missing I5, I7, and I8.

This is a task-based, within-subject event-related fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (mixed-model ANOVAs) with tabulated activation coordinates and cluster thresholds. The task requires encoding and short-term maintenance of interval durations and making duration comparisons, engaging working memory, auditory rehearsal, and decision-making (executive) processes; the authors explicitly analyze working-memory/decision (difficulty) contrasts. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis focus on executive-function domains (working memory/decision processes), provides within-group task contrasts (encoding vs baseline; hard vs easy discriminations), reports voxelwise whole-brain results in tables/figures, and uses a healthy adult participant group. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of mental calculation that probes cognitive processes including working memory and rule-based manipulation (executive functions). The study reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (fixed-effects), multiple within-group task contrasts (each condition vs result-matching baseline; direct condition comparisons), and whole-brain activation maps/tables in the text and figures. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of executive-function domains and provides within-group, voxelwise task-evoked results suitable for inclusion.

This study is excluded because it does not assess executive function or cognitive control tasks required by the review. Specifically, the fMRI paradigm involves affective face processing (fearful/angry face matching) and probes corticolimbic reactivity and connectivity, not executive domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked maps are reported), I8 (within-group task contrast: face-processing vs sensorimotor control), I9 (participant group acceptable—healthy volunteers), I10 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (fMRI/PET assessing executive function/cognitive control task) and I6 (task does not fall within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria apply (exclusion_criteria_applied: []). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study that investigated memory-guided saccadic sequences and their neural correlates. It meets I5: it is a task-based fMRI study assessing cognitive control/sequence memory. It meets I6: the paradigm engages working memory and sequence planning, which are established executive domains. It meets I7: whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses were performed using SPM99 and reported as statistical maps (Z-values, corrected thresholds). It meets I8: within-group task contrasts are reported (New vs Rest, Familiar vs Rest, New vs Familiar). It meets I9: a within-group healthy adult sample is reported. It meets I10: whole-brain results are described in the text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical work) are triggered. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an executive function. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects), including within-group task contrasts (e.g., 1-/2-/3-back vs 0-back; verbal vs spatial 3-back), with whole-brain voxelwise maps (cluster-corrected; coordinates reported). Although slice coverage omitted inferior temporal/cerebellar regions, partial-brain acquisition is allowed per criteria. Methods, results, and tables of coordinates are provided in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, within-group task contrasts of an imitation paradigm (COPY vs INCONGRUOUS, COPY vs SPATIAL) in healthy participants and reports voxelwise results with coordinates. However, the experimental task assesses perception–action matching / imitation (social sensorimotor processes) rather than an established executive function domain. Although the authors discuss working memory and error-detection processes, the tasks do not constitute classical executive-function paradigms (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) as required by the review inclusion criteria. Therefore I5 and I6 are not satisfied, while I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses fMRI (and MEG) with within-group voxelwise contrasts (conditions vs rest) and reports whole-brain group maps, but the task is passive auditory spatial attention/reorienting rather than an established executive function (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Thus it fails inclusion criterion I6 (task not within established executive function domains) and I5 (does not assess executive function/cognitive control despite being an fMRI task). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain maps reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts against rest), I9 (within-group contrasts in a participant group), I10 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain) that reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (structured vs. unstructured) with FDR-corrected thresholds and tables/figures. A within-group task contrast is reported for healthy adult participants. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study that uses a parametric verbal working memory task (an established executive function domain) with both within-group contrasts (each load vs control) and random-effects group analyses. Analyses were performed voxelwise across the whole brain using SPM2, and results are reported with stereotaxic coordinates and tables. The paper thus provides task-evoked, group-level voxelwise statistical maps and within-group task contrasts for participant groups (pre-HD and controls), meeting all inclusion criteria and violating no exclusion criteria. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing complete assessment.

This paper reports task-based fMRI experiments (N Back working memory and episodic memory paradigms) with group-level, voxelwise analyses (SPM99 random-effects) reporting whole-brain results and peak coordinates. Within-subject contrasts (Two Back vs Zero Back; encoding vs rest) were computed and used in second-level analyses. Results include SPM maps and coordinates for activations in prefrontal and medial temporal regions. Participant groups include healthy controls (and cognitive data include schizophrenia patients), satisfying applicability across groups. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory/anticipation (executive function) in schizophrenia and healthy controls. It reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps using SPM99 (fixed- and random-effects, conjunction analyses) and within-group contrasts (activation vs rest) for each group. Although slice coverage was partial (14 slices), analyses were voxelwise and group-level coordinates/figures/tables are reported. Results are presented as tables/figures with coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based working memory paradigm (executive function domain) with voxelwise, whole-brain analyses reported using SPM2. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (task vs rest and separate encoding/maintenance/retrieval contrasts), describes voxelwise group-level statistical maps and thresholds, and provides regional activation results (figures/tables referenced). Partial-brain coverage (lower cerebellum/brainstem omitted) does not preclude inclusion because analyses were voxelwise. Participants include a clinical sample (schizophrenia), which is allowed. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly examines cognitive control during a gambling/decision-making task manipulating uncertainty. It meets inclusion criteria as follows: I5 – uses task-based fMRI to assess cognitive control/executive function (decision uncertainty, resource allocation); I6 – the task probes cognitive control/conflict and decision processes (authors frame it as control-related and compare conditions of differing control demands); I7 – whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses and exploratory whole-brain contrasts are reported (maps/voxelwise contrasts and figures described); I8 – within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., uncertain wins vs probable wins, probable wins vs probable losses, all trials vs fixation); I9 – reports within-group results for a healthy adult sample (acceptable participant group); I10 – whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in text (coordinates available). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes an executive function paradigm (color-naming Stroop, an inhibition/selective-attention task) and reports voxelwise, group-level statistical maps. The paper reports a within-group random-effects one-sample t-test for the motor task in controls, and reports group-level voxelwise two-sample (bipolar vs control) random-effects analyses for both motor and Stroop contrasts. Analyses were whole-brain SPM2 voxelwise maps with cluster correction and results presented in tables/figures. Participants include clinical (bipolar) and control groups; individual subject contrasts (task vs control conditions) were computed.
