Therefore the study meets I5 (task-based fMRI including an executive task), I6 (Stroop falls in inhibition/executive domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain maps), I8 (at least one within-group task contrast reported), I9 (clinical sample allowed), and I10 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (NT vs CT) with whole-brain statistical maps (Z-statistics), cluster results, and a table of coordinates for activated regions. The methods describe preprocessing, normalization to MNI space, and group analyses; figures and Table 1 provide whole-brain activation details. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports within-group contrasts). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is an fMRI task-activation study with voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses and within-group contrasts (satisfies I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the experimental manipulation and reported contrasts probe episodic memory encoding (subsequent memory effects) and associative/recall processes rather than an executive-function or cognitive-control task falling within the specified domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Thus it does not meet I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) or I6 (task within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based PET study that directly examines voluntary emotion suppression, a form of inhibitory control engaging prefrontal executive systems. It reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (Suppression vs Attending and vice versa) using whole-brain SPM analyses and provides peak coordinates. Participants are a human sample (healthy females). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for modality (PET), task-based executive/inhibition domain, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, within-group contrasts, participant reporting, and coordinate reporting.

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/NoGo), which falls within executive function (inhibition). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (nogo vs. go) with whole-brain random-effects analyses (main effect thresholded p<.05 FWE) and provides coordinate tables and statistical maps for results. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for task activation meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that probes top-down attentional control and deliberate shifts of attentional set between feature dimensions. The paradigm directly assesses cognitive control/set-shifting (cognitive flexibility), an established executive-function domain. The study reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (e.g., shift vs hold) analyzed with a random-effects GLM across whole-brain volumes and provides Talairach coordinates and figures of activations. Participants are healthy adults and the paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study used a task-based, within-group word-retrieval (verbal fluency/word generation) paradigm that engages executive processes (initiation, search, sustained attention/working memory). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects, voxelwise group analyses (task vs baseline and difficulty contrasts) with coordinates and figures, meeting requirements for group-level voxelwise maps. Participants are a defined within-group (healthy adults). Results and methods are fully reported (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for executive-function-related activation (initiation/attention), whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and within-group contrasts.

The full text reports an original, task-based fMRI study using a modified Stroop (inhibition/cognitive control) task, meeting executive-function domain requirements. The paper performed voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (one-sample t-tests within patients and controls and between-group two-sample t-tests) using SPM99 and reports clusters/coordinates and a figure of activation. A within-group contrast (interference vs facilitation) is explicitly reported for both groups, with tables of regions and voxelwise correlation analyses. Therefore inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is an empirical fMRI task study of visuospatial working memory/attention shifting (executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task activation analyses (random-effects model) with whole-brain (cluster-level corrected) results and coordinates/tables/figures, and presents within-group task contrasts (Rotation+Arrow, Rotation, Arrow, and Rotation+Arrow vs Rotation/Arrow). Although SEM connectivity is also reported, activation maps are clearly provided. Participant sample and methods are described in full. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain fMRI executive-function activations and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of auditory temporal discrimination/timing, not an executive function or cognitive control task as defined by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the paper reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (easy–baseline, difficult–baseline, difficult–easy), meeting several inclusion criteria, it does not assess an executive function domain (I5 and I6 are not satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI task study using a counting Stroop (inhibition/response conflict) paradigm with button-press responses. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level activation contrasts (Stroop vs control) with whole-brain cluster correction and provides tables/figures of significant clusters. Although slice coverage is limited (19 sagittal slices), analyses were voxelwise and thus satisfy the partial-brain allowance. A within-group task contrast is clearly reported for healthy adult participants. Functional connectivity analyses are also present but do not preclude inclusion since task activation maps are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I5–I10 and qualifies for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based modified Stroop paradigm (selective attention/inhibition), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (SPM99; second-level random effects), with within-group contrasts of task versus rest for both healthy controls and schizophrenia patients. Results are presented as SPM maps and coordinate tables. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study; within-group contrasts are reported). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study of mental arithmetic that explicitly manipulates task complexity to tax working memory. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (complex vs. simple) using SPM2 with FDR correction and presents conjunction and contrast results in tables and figures. The within-group contrasts (complex > simple for each operator) are reported and used in group-level analyses. Tasks target working memory/executive demands (explicitly discussed) and thus fall within the executive function domain. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study with group-level, voxelwise analyses reporting whole-brain activation maps and contrasts. The serial prediction task requires encoding and monitoring sequential patterns, engaging working memory/vigilance and attentional prediction processes (executive domains). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (when/what/where vs control and direct contrasts among conditions), voxelwise group analyses (one-sample t tests), and whole-brain results in tables/figures. Participants are a healthy adult group. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI task study that directly examines cognitive control processes (ACC conflict detection, right DLPFC monitoring) during a two-alternative associative recognition task. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM), including within-group task contrasts (Strong > Weak; Weak > Strong), with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults and results are fully reported in methods, results, tables, and discussion. Although the primary paradigm is episodic associative recognition, the paper explicitly tests and interprets executive/cognitive control mechanisms (conflict monitoring, familiarity monitoring) — functions that fall within established executive domains (monitoring/inhibition/selective attention). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study examining predicting/working-memory processes (executive function domain). It reports within-group voxelwise group analyses (random-effects SPM results) contrasting Predict vs Detect (and Predict vs Detect 3-back), with whole-brain results presented (figures and coordinate table). Participants are healthy adults. All required information (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and include within-group contrasts. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a Go/No Go inhibition paradigm (executive function), with group-level, voxelwise SPM2 random-effects analyses and reported within-group contrasts (errors and correct rejects) for both OCD and control groups. Whole-brain preprocessing/normalization was performed and results are reported as voxel coordinates and figures; small-volume correction was applied to ROIs but voxelwise task-activation maps and coordinate tables are provided. Participants include a clinical sample (OCD) and matched controls. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI task-based study that includes a working-memory (episodic/working memory) paradigm, which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., EWM > SM) for both healthy controls and AD subjects, with group-level SPM analyses and reported activation coordinates (tables/coordinates), corrected for multiple comparisons. Acquisition used slice-based EPI and voxelwise whole-brain normalization/analysis (partial-brain acquisition would still qualify). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study of visuo-spatial working memory (an executive function: working memory). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (fixed- and random-effects), within-group task contrasts (various task vs. grid/no-grid conditions and baseline), and presents group statistical maps/tables/figures. Although coverage was partial (parieto-frontal and occipito-temporo-frontal scans), analyses were voxelwise at the group level, satisfying partial-brain requirements. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise group maps; partial coverage acceptable), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a Stroop task (inhibition/interference), which falls within executive function domains. The study reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM) with random-effects group-level contrasts and provides coordinates and cluster results. Within-group task contrasts are reported for patients (task vs control/interference vs control) and for controls, and pre/post within-patient contrasts are also presented. Participant sample (clinical OCD and healthy controls) is acceptable per criteria. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided, allowing extraction of whole-brain task activation coordinates. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of a numerical Stroop (number-size congruity) task that probes interference/inhibition and attentional control (executive function). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., incongruent > congruent, distance effects) with tables of coordinates and figures, and within-group contrasts versus baseline and between conditions. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures descriptions) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this study reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI contrasts (Ambiguous vs Unambiguous) and within-group analyses, its primary focus is language comprehension and lexical ambiguity rather than an explicit executive function task. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not assess executive function/cognitive control as a primary task-based paradigm), I6 (tasks do not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation; although working memory capacity was measured and inhibition/suppression is discussed, the paradigm itself is a sentence-reading language task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be excluded from an executive-function meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of attentional control (Stroop), which falls within executive function/inhibition. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise statistical analyses (voxel-wise repeated-measures ANOVA and blocked voxelwise maps converted to Z-scores) and provides whole-brain activation results (tables of Talairach coordinates and figures). Within-group task contrasts are reported (incongruent vs. neutral; incongruent-eligible vs. incongruent-ineligible), and participants are healthy adults. Although acquisition used limited slices (partial-brain coverage), the study performed voxelwise group analyses and reported whole-brain-style results, which meets the review’s allowance for partial-brain acquisitions so long as voxelwise analyses are presented. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The article reports a task-based fMRI study of fluid reasoning/cognitive flexibility (matrix reasoning adaptation), meeting the executive-function domain (cognitive flexibility). The abstract states a mixed-effects analysis corrected for multiple comparisons and a 2×2 ANOVA reporting task-difficulty and response-correctness effects, indicating group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts. Participants are not exclusionary. Reporting of whole-brain results is described in the text. However, the supplied full text appears incomplete (core methods/results/discussion sections are not present in the provided HTML), so confirmation of details (e.g., exact voxelwise maps or coordinate tables) is limited. Therefore I include the study but flag the full text as incomplete and assign moderate confidence.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control (cognitive reappraisal) using a task-based paradigm. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses (thresholded, coordinates in tables/figures) and within-group task contrasts (increase>look; decrease>look), with adult participants. Results include whole-brain activations and small-volume amygdala analyses but are not limited to ROIs. Therefore it satisfies I5 (fMRI cognitive control task), I6 (task involves cognitive control/executive processes such as interference resolution/inhibition/working-memory-like processes), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain group maps reported), I8 (within-group contrasts reported), I9 (participants reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study (AX-CPT variant) examining cognitive control/attentional set shifting and reward expectation. It reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (FDR-corrected) and presents group-level task contrasts (reward expectancy, verbal/spatial bias, all-tasks-vs-rest) with coordinates and figures. The task falls within executive function domains (vigilance/monitoring, cognitive flexibility/attention control). Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so full text is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria (none of E3–E6).

This study is an empirical fMRI paper with whole-brain voxelwise group analyses and within-group contrasts (approximate vs control, exact vs control, magnitude comparison vs baseline) and reports coordinates—thus it meets I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the tasks are numerical processing (symbolic exact/approximate calculation and non-symbolic magnitude comparison) aimed at number representation and arithmetic development, not tasks that fall within established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not satisfy I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) nor I6 (tasks within executive function domains), so it must be excluded. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study that reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain activation contrasts. The task involves divided attention with a verbal memory (working memory) component and attention-switching/divided-attention demands, fitting established executive domains (working memory/cognitive flexibility). The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (within-night experimental vs. baseline contrasts), cluster-thresholded whole-brain maps and tables, and regression analyses relating performance to activation. Participants are healthy adults but any participant group is acceptable. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study probing voluntary control/choice of attentional orienting, which falls under cognitive control/executive function (initiation/volitional control). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-thresholded corrected maps) and within-group contrasts (choice > instructed, instructed > choice, etc.). Participants are healthy adults and results (including coordinates and ROI/whole-brain findings) are reported in the main text. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study (simultaneous EEG–fMRI) using a mental arithmetic task that engages working memory/attention (executive domain). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM99 analyses with group-level one-sample t tests on task-related regressors (state-related boxcar arithmetic vs rest) and PSI-related regressors, and presents coordinates/tables/figures (Table 1, Figs. 5–7). A within-group task contrast (arithmetic vs rest) is explicitly analyzed and reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation in executive function domains, with whole-brain voxelwise, group-level results clearly described in text/tables/figures. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This article reports a task-based fMRI study (Multi-Source Interference Task) probing cognitive control/executive function in both healthy and opiate-dependent participants. It includes whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (within-group I>C contrasts reported for controls and opiate users, with cluster-wise correction and figures/tables) and reports metabolite and behaviour associations. All core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation meta-analysis of executive function.

This is an fMRI task study of cognitive control (meets I5, I6) with within-group task contrasts reported and a healthy participant sample (meets I8 and I9). However, the imaging analyses reported are restricted to a priori ROI analyses (ACC and lPFC) rather than group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation maps. The paper does not report voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses or coordinate tables for such maps, so it fails I7 and therefore meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) comparing individuals with schizophrenia and controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (task–fixation and onset-transient correlations), and presents within-group task contrasts and regional time courses for each group. Tasks include working memory (2-back), encoding, and recognition — all within executive/cognitive domains. Whole-brain coverage and voxelwise analyses are described; results are reported in figures, tables, and text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cross-modal attention shifts that probes executive control processes (cognitive flexibility and inhibition). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and pairwise contrasts) with cluster-correction, and presents within-group task contrasts (Focus-Auditory, Focus-Visual, Shift; task>baseline and Shift>Focus). Results are reported as voxelwise maps, tables, and figures for both older and younger groups. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes an executive function task (2-back working memory) and recognition (episodic) tasks (I5,I6). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level GLM contrasts with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction and reported coordinates/ROIs (I7,I10). Within-group contrasts (task vs fixation and material contrasts) are reported (I8). Participant groups are healthy adults (acceptable per I9). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study probing top-down attentional control (dynamic ‘zooming in’/‘zooming out’ of attention), which the authors frame as a cognitive control/top–down attentional control process. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM2) with cluster-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of coordinates. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., zooming in > HLB, zooming out > HLB, in > out), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable sample). The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that investigates memory-related processes during a continuation paradigm and explicitly reports recruitment of a classic prefrontal–parietal–temporal working memory network during the continuation/delay phase. Analyses are whole-brain, random-effects, voxelwise, with reported group-level contrasts (e.g., Continuation vs Pacing, Pattern effects) and coordinate tables/figures. Thus it provides within-group task activation maps relevant to the executive function domain of working memory and meets the meta-analysis requirements.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (SPM2) with group-level, voxelwise analyses and whole-brain coverage reporting peak coordinate tables. The task explicitly probes executive domains relevant to the review (action planning, monitoring/vigilance, rule processing, initiation/stopping), and reports within-group contrasts (e.g., action planning > coasting, monitoring traffic > coasting, traffic rules > coasting). Results are reported as voxelwise group t-tests with coordinates (Tables), satisfying reporting requirements. Participants are a within-group adult sample (licensed taxi drivers). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables) is provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study that investigates conflict related to goal selection and bimanual movement planning — processes of cognitive control/response selection. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses (e.g., incongruent vs congruent contrasts, symbolic vs spatial), with tables and figures describing activation loci (clusterwise correction reported). Healthy adult within-group contrasts are reported. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI addressing cognitive control/conflict), I6 (task probes executive/cognitive-control processes—response selection/conflict, mapping onto inhibition/cognitive control domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (healthy participant group included), and I10 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (game > dot, game > scene, game > random) assessing working memory and recognition tasks in chess players — the game > dot contrast isolates working-memory/executive processes. Whole-brain images were acquired and SPM99 voxelwise group-level maps (corrected p<.05) and activation foci are reported. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-based fMRI of executive function with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts. Although the group analysis used a fixed-effects model and the sample is small (n=5), the inclusion criteria do not exclude fixed-effects or small samples. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an fMRI task study with group-level voxelwise contrasts, but the tasks probe semantic/autobiographic temporal-order and spatial-location memory retrieval rather than established executive-function domains. Although the authors discuss working-memory involvement, the primary manipulation targets episodic/semantic memory processes, not explicit executive functions (working memory paradigms like n-back, inhibition, task switching, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Therefore it does not meet I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) nor I6 (tasks within established executive domains). The paper does satisfy voxelwise whole-brain analyses (I7), reports within-group task contrasts (I8), includes an acceptable participant group (I9), and reports coordinate and map results in text/figures (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm probing spatial working memory (an executive function). The paper reports within-group voxelwise SPM analyses (SWT vs VMT) for both healthy controls and PD patients, including voxelwise statistical maps and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. It therefore meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations (I5,I6) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I7), within-group contrasts (I8), acceptable participant groups including clinical samples (I9), and reporting of voxelwise results in text/tables/figures (I10). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study with whole-brain, voxelwise within-group task contrasts (ambiguity vs risk) and reports coordinates and methods in full. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task-based study), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/figures). However, the primary experimental paradigm is economic decision-making under risk and ambiguity rather than a canonical executive-function task. Although the authors discuss executive/control processes (contextual analysis, inhibition), the task does not clearly fall within the specified executive function domains listed in I6 (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based, empirical fMRI study that directly examines selection/initiation and preparatory processes for action and includes working-memory demands for self-selection, fitting executive function domains (initiation, selection, working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (thresholded statistical maps and conjunctions), within-group contrasts (observation vs self-selection and task vs baseline), and provides voxelwise results in tables/figures. Although slice coverage was limited (17 axial slices), analyses were voxelwise and therefore satisfy the partial-coverage allowance. The full text (abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study of conflict resolution/cognitive control (executive function). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs congruent; high vs low conflict resolution) at the group level, provides whole-brain and ROI analyses with reported coordinates, and includes healthy adult participants. All inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of antisaccade and refixation tasks (BOLD fMRI), directly assessing inhibitory control (an executive function). The paper reports within-group voxelwise analyses (random-effects t maps) for refixation and antisaccade contrasts, provides whole-brain voxelwise results with Talairach coordinates, and includes clinical (schizophrenia) and control groups. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition task within executive function), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (clinical participant group allowed), and I10 (whole-brain results described with coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a GO–NOGO paradigm that assesses action planning and response selection/inhibition — an established executive function domain (inhibition). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts (e.g., NOGO vs GO) with coordinate tables and contrast images, satisfying voxelwise reporting even though Experiment 2 used reduced slice coverage. Within-group task contrasts are explicitly reported. Participants are neurologically healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a delayed-match-to-sample working-memory task (executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise within-subject and group-level analyses using SPM99, produces whole-brain parametric maps, bootstrap and permutation tests, and reports Talairach coordinates and brain figures. Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level, within-group task contrasts and whole-brain results in tables/figures. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

The study uses task-based fMRI and reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (PLS) with within-group contrasts and coordinate tables, but the experimental task is episodic memory (encoding/recognition of unfamiliar faces), not an executive function or cognitive control task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task study), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (coordinates/results clearly reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (task does NOT fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails I6 (task domain mismatch).

Although this is an event-related fMRI, whole-brain, task-based empirical study reporting group-level voxelwise contrasts (decision-making vs control; risky vs safe; wins vs losses) in healthy participants, it does not meet the meta-analysis’s task-domain requirement. The Iowa Gambling Task (IGT) is primarily a decision-making/affective learning paradigm rather than one of the specified executive-function domains listed in I6 (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Thus criterion I6 is not satisfied. I5 is borderline: while the study uses fMRI and an experimental task, the primary focus is affective decision-making rather than canonical cognitive-control/executive functions as defined by the review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered; the full text is complete. Therefore the study is excluded for failure to meet the domain-specific inclusion criterion (I6) (and I5 is not clearly satisfied under the review’s definition).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of task switching (cognitive flexibility), reporting group-level voxelwise activation maps (whole-brain acquisition and SPM96 analyses) and within-group contrasts (switching vs baseline; main effects of timing and task-order). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and tables/figures of peaks. Thus all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (fMRI task-based executive function; task within executive domains; whole-brain voxelwise group analyses; within-group task contrasts; participant group qualifies; voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (only ROI/connectivity/between-group-only/non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of thought suppression, which constitutes an executive-control/inhibition paradigm. The paper reports within-group voxelwise, group-level statistical contrasts (e.g., SUPPRESS vs FREE-THOUGHT; CLEAR vs FREE-THOUGHT) analyzed with SPM99 and thresholded t-maps, with whole-brain coverage. Participants are healthy adults and results are described at the group level (brain regions/BA reported). Thus the study satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (letter vs visuospatial decision tasks) in healthy participants. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts with coordinates and corrected statistics (task vs baseline and task vs task), satisfying within-group task contrasts. Tasks probe executive processes (response selection, inhibition, conflict monitoring), and results are reported as coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical neuroimaging research. Full text appears to include introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an n-back working memory paradigm (an established executive function domain) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects SPM99 second-level results, corrected thresholds). It includes within-group task contrasts (e.g. 2-back > 1-back) and reports whole-brain effects (tables/figures) including interactions of load × visibility in LOC. Participants are healthy volunteers and results are suitable for pooling. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study examining dynamic manipulation of auditory imagery that explicitly taxes working memory/central executive processes, meeting the executive-function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (word reversal vs baseline, rhyme judgment vs baseline, and word reversal minus rhyme judgment) with activation coordinates, tables and figures. Participants are a within-group sample of 12 healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. Although ROI/small-volume corrections are additionally reported, whole-brain voxelwise results are provided, so exclusion criteria for ROI-only or connectivity-only studies do not apply. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and does not violate E3–E6.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a Stroop paradigm (a canonical inhibition/cognitive control executive task). It reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs congruent; error vs correct) with coordinates and conjunction analyses. Participants are healthy adults and the paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study using the Stroop task (inhibition/cognitive control) with drug-free depressed patients and healthy controls. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses (univariate contrasts: incongruent vs congruent) and within-group task contrasts, with whole-brain preprocessing and second-level SPM analyses. Although the paper also presents DCM connectivity analyses, it clearly includes task activation maps and within-group contrasts suitable for pooling. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study that uses the antisaccade task (inhibition), an executive function domain. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain group analyses (t-statistics computed per voxel, Talairach normalization, corrected thresholds) and within-group contrasts (prosaccades, antisaccades, antisaccades vs prosaccades; task vs fixation), with results described in the text and figures. Participants include healthy controls and unaffected siblings. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (healthy adult participant group with within-group contrasts), I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (although the study uses fMRI, it does not assess executive function/cognitive control as the main focus; tasks are reading-aloud and lexical-decision tailored to language/phonological processing), I6 (tasks do not fall within established executive-function domains such as working memory, inhibition as primary task, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation—lexical decision/reading are language tasks even if secondary inhibitory demands are discussed). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement that the paradigm assesses executive function/cognitive control (I5 and I6).

This study reports task-based fMRI (and EEG) of an executive function task (intradimensional/extradimensional rule shifts; cognitive flexibility). It includes within-group, voxelwise whole-brain group-level contrasts (negative>positive feedback for ID and ED conditions) analyzed with SPM2 and reported with coordinates and cluster results. The task falls within executive function/cognitive control (cognitive flexibility), and whole-brain voxelwise analyses and ROI analyses are described. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of task-evoked executive function activations. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures) is provided and appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI with simultaneous EEG during a mental arithmetic task designed to induce working memory load (an executive function). It includes within-group, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses contrasting mental arithmetic vs reference, and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and multiple comparison correction (FWE/FDR). Although acquisition used 20 slices, the analysis was voxelwise at the group level, which meets the allowance for partial-brain acquisition. Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study probing selection/cognitive control (free vs externally specified selection), which maps onto executive function processes. It reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (random-effects second-level t-tests) with whole-brain results and tables/figures of activation peaks and SPM maps (including whole-brain family-wise error corrected results and coordinate tables). Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., free selection vs external specification; FA−EA; FC−EC; action vs colour), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. The sample and methods are clearly described and the full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). All applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10).

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting group-level, voxelwise task activation maps (SPM99) for rule-based vs similarity-based categorization. The tasks explicitly engage executive processes (working memory, selective attention, response monitoring) and compare conditions within groups (Rule vs Similarity; task effects vs baseline). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholds, Talairach coordinates, activation tables/figures). Participants are a healthy volunteer group (within-group contrasts reported). Results are presented as coordinate tables and figures, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that includes a sustained visual attention (vigilance) task alongside an episodic retrieval task. It meets I5 (fMRI task-based study of cognitive control/attention) and I6 (vigilance falls within the listed executive function domains). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses using SPM99 (I7), and presents within-group task contrasts (ER vs baseline, VA vs baseline, direct ER vs VA contrasts; I8). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy young adults (I9). Whole-brain results are reported in tables and figures and described in text (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and include within-group contrasts rather than only between-group effects. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations (vigilance/sustained attention).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that probes sustained and shifting spatial attention using event-related designs and behaviorally validated vigilance (counting near-threshold target dims) — which maps onto the ‘vigilance’ executive domain. It reports group-level, voxelwise/ surface-based statistical maps with permutation cluster correction and provides peak coordinates (Table 1) and within-group task contrasts (shift vs baseline; maintenance vs catch; overt vs covert). Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are presented. Therefore it satisfies the required inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This study reports original event-related fMRI data (BOLD) in 16 healthy adults performing a task-switching paradigm assessing cognitive flexibility, an executive function. It includes voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses and reports within-group contrasts (object-switch vs rule-switch and others), with whole-brain results and ROI supplemental analyses. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based neuroimaging of executive function and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of negative priming, a phenomenon closely related to inhibitory components of executive control. The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (repetition-ignored vs control) analyzed with SPM2 at the group level, including both an a priori ROI analysis (SVC) and an exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analysis with reported peak coordinates. Behavioral and imaging results are presented along with methods, results, and discussion in full. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task assessing executive function/inhibition), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of attentional control (Stroop-like interference), which falls within executive function domains (inhibition/selection). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group random-effects analyses (interference vs control) and presents whole-brain results in text, figures, and tables. Although slice coverage was limited (15 slices), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted, satisfying partial-brain allowance. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an EEG/ERP study (with fMRI results referenced from a prior study) that does not report original task-based fMRI or PET whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps. Although it contains within-group task contrasts (attend vs interpret) and uses healthy participant data, it does not satisfy the primary modality requirement for this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (within-group task contrast present) and I9 (participant group reported; within-group analyses performed). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not an fMRI or PET task-based study reporting original fMRI/PET results), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked group-level statistical maps reported). I6 (task domain) is borderline: the task is visual-spatial attentional orienting which is related to attention/vigilance but is not clearly one of the explicitly listed executive domains; therefore I6 is not confidently met for purposes of this review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) directly apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive attention/control (Stroop variants) with group-level voxelwise activation maps comparing incongruent vs. neutral trials (a within-group task contrast). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses, peak coordinates, and figures, and describes methods, subjects, and results (intro, methods, results, discussion present). Although acquisition used 15 slices (partial coverage), analyses were voxelwise and reported at the group level, which is acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical PET study using task-based paradigms (translation and language switching) that probe cognitive control (inhibition and cognitive flexibility). The study reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM and reports coordinates/tables for within-group contrasts (translation vs reading; switching vs no switching). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy bilingual adults. Results are presented as voxelwise activation maps and tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM) reporting within-group contrasts (CA minus FR, FR minus CA) and tables/figures of activation. Although the paradigm is framed as category learning, the tasks explicitly involve maintenance and application of learned rules, working memory and attentional/control processes (rule maintenance, target monitoring, selection), which fall within established executive function domains (working memory/cognitive control). Participants are a healthy adult group and within-group contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/attentional control over threat-related distractors (executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (voxel-wise comparisons with whole-brain correction and ROI small-volume corrections) and provides coordinates for activations. Key reported contrasts are within-group task contrasts (threat-related vs neutral distractor trials; start trials vs others) and regressions against state anxiety. Participants are healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROI/SVC results (whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported), is not solely connectivity/resting analyses, includes within-group contrasts (not only between-group), and is empirical data (not a review). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is a task-based fMRI study (3T) reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (complex g-task > simple g-task) using one-sample and two-sample random effects analyses and regression, with coordinates and thresholding reported. The paradigm elicits fronto-parietal activations tied to cognitive control processes (working memory/attention, reasoning/problem solving) and the authors explicitly link findings to working memory and cognitive control networks. It therefore meets criteria for fMRI task-based executive/cognitive-control investigation, contains within-group task contrasts, reports whole-brain voxelwise results, and is applicable across participant groups (adolescent sample). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. No exclusion criteria apply. Overall confidence is high that the study fits the meta-analysis objective of pooling executive-function task activations.

The study reports an empirical task-based fMRI investigation using an emotional go/nogo paradigm, which falls squarely within the inhibition domain of executive function. Methods describe whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM analyses and contrasts (e.g., target vs nontarget; nontarget vs target) with random-effects group maps and cluster correction, satisfying the requirement for voxelwise within-group task contrasts. Results present voxelwise activation findings (amygdala, caudate, ventral striatum, inferior frontal gyrus, ACC) and correlations with behavior. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and it is an empirical human neuroimaging study. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study with whole-brain voxelwise group analyses and within-group contrasts (insight vs non-insight) in healthy participants, but the task (compound remote associate problems; insight/creative problem solving) does not fall within the review's specified executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study, task-based), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis with reported group-level statistics/coordinates), I8 (within-group task contrast: insight vs noninsight; main effect of task also reported), I9 (within-group healthy participant sample qualifies), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Excluded because it does not meet I6: task is not within established executive function domains required by the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study using a task (negative priming) that indexes inhibitory control, an established executive-function domain (inhibition). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise second-level random-effects contrasts (NeuI>C, NegI>C, NegI>NeuI) analyzed with SPM2 and provides whole-brain activation results with MNI coordinates (Table 2, figures). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Although the sample is small (n=8), that does not violate inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of reversal learning, which assesses cognitive flexibility/affective switching — an executive function domain. The study reports within-group, group-level random-effects voxelwise contrasts (e.g., CR > BL, PENS+PRE > BL, FRE > BL, FRE > PENS+PRE) analyzed with SPM2 and reports whole-brain results with MNI coordinates in tables/figures. Participants are healthy volunteers and within-group contrasts are provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This empirical fMRI study investigates cued task switching (an executive-function cognitive flexibility paradigm) using a task-based design in healthy participants. The authors report group-level, voxelwise analyses (subject contrast maps followed by random-effects one-sample t-tests) to identify activations and define ROIs; they also report within-group task contrasts (e.g., switch > repeat, task conditions vs null events, and motor contrasts). Whole-brain voxelwise results were used to select ROIs, and the manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a Stroop task to probe attentional control/executive function (inhibition/selection). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, mixed-effects group analyses (FLAME) with whole-brain cluster-based inference and tables of peak coordinates for contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs neutral; one-word vs four-word). Tasks clearly fall within executive function domains (inhibition/cognitive control). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses comparing task conditions (linguistic vs control) within healthy adult groups. Although the tasks are phonological, the paper explicitly manipulates and reports working-memory/monitoring and selection demands (sequence vs single comparisons, pseudoword effects) and interprets frontal activation in terms of working memory/monitoring (executive function). Analyses include within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise ANOVAs with reported coordinates/tables and figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for an executive-function meta-analysis (working memory domain) and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study of deductive reasoning that examines inhibition of belief-bias (an executive/inhibitory control process). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM99 with random effects and voxel-level correction, and presents within-group contrasts (e.g., reasoning vs baseline; correct inhibitory trials vs incorrect inhibitory trials). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI (I5, I6), whole-brain voxelwise reporting (I7), within-group contrasts (I8), broad participant eligibility (I9), and acceptable reporting of voxelwise results (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a task-based go–nogo paradigm (inhibition domain of executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FSL FLAME mixed-effects, cluster-thresholded Z images) and within-group contrasts (go vs nogo, compatibility interactions). Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. Results (voxelwise activations) are described in text and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (image acquisition, preprocessing, first- and second-level analyses), Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activation mapping and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of transitive inference (TI) that probes manipulation/integration of learned information—processes the authors frame as executive (prefrontal) operations beyond simple short-term memory. The study uses fMRI (satisfies I5), and the cognitive operation (reasoning requiring manipulation/integration of facts) maps onto established executive functions (working memory/executive manipulation and related planning/cognitive control processes), so I consider I6 met. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and thresholded statistical maps (TI–HT and HT–VIS contrasts) with tables of coordinates and figures (I7 and I10 met). It includes within-group task contrasts (TI vs HT and HT vs VIS) at the group level (I8 met). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (I9 met). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, and this is an original empirical activation study (E3–E6 not met). Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures, tables).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of an antisaccade task (inhibition), which is an established executive function (inhibition). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level mixed-effects statistical parametric maps contrasting antisaccade vs prosaccade (within-group contrasts), includes tables of Talairach coordinates and figures of maps/time courses, and uses whole-voxel GLM/deconvolution rather than ROI-only analyses. Although imaging used limited axial slice coverage, the protocol and analyses are voxelwise and partial-brain acquisition is acceptable per criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria.

The study reports both EEG and fMRI experiments and includes a group-level, voxelwise within-group contrast (insight preparation vs. noninsight preparation) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and cluster thresholds. However, the task is a compound remote-associates (insight/creativity) problem paradigm rather than a canonical executive-function task within the prespecified domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors interpret ACC activity as reflecting cognitive control, the task itself does not clearly fall within the listed executive-function domains (I6 not met). Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study that includes an executive-control task (reverse alphabetizing) designed to engage working-memory manipulation and monitoring, meeting I5 and I6. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level multivariate ST-PLS results with voxelwise maps, figures, and tables of local maxima (peak coordinates and cluster extents), satisfying I7 and I10. The analysis includes within-group task contrasts (e.g., EM retrieval vs Alpha; recency vs recognition) and within-group PLS analyses as described, meeting I8. Participant groups (young and older adults) are reported, satisfying I9. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be included for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a Stroop color-word interference task (an executive function/inhibition paradigm) and reports task-evoked, within-group voxelwise activation analyses. The paper describes group-level statistical maps (incongruent vs. neutral contrast, corrected P<0.001) transformed to stereotactic space for multisubject comparisons, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Participants were healthy adults; at least one within-group contrast is reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical work) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study using the counting Stroop (a well-established inhibition/cognitive-control executive task). It provides whole-brain, voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., number Stroop vs neutral during no-stimulation) and reports activation coordinates; within-group task contrasts are explicitly analyzed. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly assesses planning and initiation of motor sequences—domains classified under executive function (planning, initiation). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise ANOVAs, HRF estimates, Talairach coordinates) with results presented in tables and figures. Within-group task contrasts are reported (IG vs EG, premovement vs movement, complexity effects; main effects vs baseline), and healthy volunteers are the participant group. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported as coordinates/ROIs. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text appears complete. Therefore, the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study investigating working memory (spatial vs nonspatial) during language comprehension. It reports group-level, voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses (SPM2) including within-group contrasts (e.g., Space > Nonspace), whole-brain thresholds (FWE-corrected and uncorrected) and tables/figures of activations. Tasks map to the executive domain 'working memory'. Participants are healthy volunteers. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that examines executive functions during serial-arithmetic dual- and single-task conditions. It clearly assesses executive processes (working memory, response selection/inhibition, task coordination), uses whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses (random-effects), and reports within-group task contrasts (each arithmetic condition vs baseline; dual vs single contrasts). Whole-brain results are presented in tables of Talairach coordinates and figures. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods (participants, design, MRI acquisition, analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete.

Full text presents an fMRI task with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts (wins vs losses; high vs low provocation) and reports coordinates (satisfies I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However the task is a Taylor Aggression Paradigm designed to elicit reactive aggression and social-emotional processes rather than an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although authors discuss cognitive control/conflict monitoring, the paradigm does not fall within the predefined executive-function task categories required by I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (task domain).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (cued global/local selective attention/conflict task) in healthy adults. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level analyses (SPM'99 random-effects ANOVA; voxelwise F-map used to define dACC ROI), and contrasts isolating conflict (incongruent vs congruent targets) and cue-related activity (cue-only vs cue-plus-target). Whole-brain voxelwise results are described and illustrated. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/conflict (size-congruity Stroop-like paradigm) that reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (random-effects, p'<.05 corrected) and within-group contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; congruent vs neutral). Results are reported as coordinates, tables and figures and include functional connectivity as supplementary analyses. The task probes executive function/inhibition/conflict monitoring, satisfying the review objective. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of voluntary self-regulation of slow cortical potentials (SCPs), which the authors interpret as involving cognitive control processes including active inhibition and preparatory attention. It therefore assesses executive/cognitive control (I5) and maps onto established executive domains (inhibition/initiative/attention) as discussed in the text (I6). The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses with both fixed- and random-effects group-level contrasts (I7), and includes within-group task contrasts (negativity vs baseline/passive viewing, positivity vs baseline, and negativity vs positivity) (I8). Participant groups include both healthy subjects and epilepsy patients with within-group contrasts reported (I9). Results are presented as tables/figures with coordinates and detailed descriptions (I10). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-group voxelwise task activation contrasts during a lexical decision task and interprets left mid-dorsolateral and medial prefrontal activations as reflecting executive control/inhibitory processes. The paper provides whole-brain analyses (voxelwise contrasts, corrected cluster thresholds), within-group contrasts (lexicality, neighborhood size, interaction, parametric analyses), and participant details (healthy adult sample). Results are reported in text, tables, and figures, and the full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of inhibition (GO/NOGO), an executive function domain. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps (voxelwise t-tests with voxelwise thresholds and Talairach-normalized %AUC maps) and describes within-group contrasts (high vs low conflict condition within young participants) as well as group analyses. Results are reported in text/tables and figures. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that assesses attentional/visuo-attentional processing (selective/sustained attention), a domain covered by the meta-analysis (vigilance/attention as executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses (whole-brain and masked visual-cortex analyses), presents within-group task contrasts (e.g. Age > Colour) for controls and AD, and provides whole-brain results in tables/figures. Participant groups include both healthy controls and a clinical AD sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, enabling application of inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a modified Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (set-shifting) that targets cognitive flexibility — an executive function. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM99 random-effects GLM) with multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., A minus D, A minus B, B minus C) and provides Talairach/MNI coordinates and statistical maps. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Reporting includes tables, figures, methods, results, and discussion, satisfying whole-text completeness. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for pooling executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that examines attention-related processing during an auditory goal-directed task (subjects detect motion of footsteps). The paradigm manipulates attention/vigilance and involves response selection, fitting an executive-domain task (vigilance/attentional control). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise task contrast maps (footstep minus rest) and provides whole-brain cluster coordinates and t-values (Table 1), satisfying voxelwise evidence and coordinate reporting. At least one within-group task contrast is reported and used for analyses. Results are reported in the main text (methods, results, tables), and the study is not limited to ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables).

This fMRI study used a mood induction paradigm (happy/sad) with a gender-discrimination control. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (sadness–cognition, happiness–cognition, sadness–happiness) analyzed with SPM99, satisfying I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the tasks probe emotional/mood induction and simple gender discrimination rather than established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met. No exclusion criteria apply (E3–E6 not met). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it does not assess executive function/cognitive control tasks as required (I5, I6 not satisfied).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly investigates cognitive control/conflict (processing of semantic–prosodic incongruence) using a within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analysis. Group-level random-effects SPM2 contrasts are reported (e.g., CONF vs NOCONF, main effect vs baseline), with whole-brain correction and voxelwise inference. The paradigm requires overriding task-irrelevant semantic information to identify prosody (inhibition/response selection), which maps onto executive function domains. Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task study with whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (semantic categorization > passive listening) in healthy adults, so it meets I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the experimental task is a language-based semantic categorization/target-detection paradigm intended to probe bottom-up vs top-down language processing, not an established executive function or cognitive-control task as defined by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The semantic categorization here primarily probes language/semantic processes rather than core executive domains; the authors do not frame the task as testing inhibition, working memory, set-shifting, planning, initiation, or sustained vigilance. Therefore it fails I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM) and coordinates, including within-group contrasts (main effect of condition, main effect of velocity, regression analyses).
