Although the primary paradigm probes smooth pursuit eye movements, the contrast of target blanking versus continuous presentation was explicitly designed to engage extraretinal mechanisms such as prediction, monitoring and short-/mid-term spatial working memory (DLPFC, angular gyrus)—functions within established executive domains (working memory/monitoring). Participants were healthy adults and results are reported as group-level voxelwise maps with tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and should be INCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI during an emotional Stroop task that requires inhibition/cognitive control (suppressing word meaning to name ink color), which falls within the executive function domain of inhibition. The paper includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FEAT/FLAME, voxelwise contrasts with cluster-size correction via AlphaSim) and reports within-group contrasts (negative vs. neutral; positive vs. neutral; task vs. fixation) with coordinates and cluster descriptions. Participant groups are nonpatient undergraduates (acceptable per criteria). Results are presented as voxelwise maps and clusters/coordinates, meeting the requirement that whole-brain evidence may be reported in tables/figures/text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study reports original human fMRI data including a counting Stroop task (an inhibition/interference paradigm within executive function). It carries out group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (fixed-effect group analyses) with statistical parametric maps and reports coordinates/tables (FWER-corrected). Within-group contrasts are reported (counting vs rest; neutral and interference conditions). Participant groups are described (control group of healthy females) and results are presented for within-group contrasts. Therefore it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive/inhibition task), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study using a task-based paradigm that probes cognitive control processes (go/no-go inhibition, response-selection, conflict/facilitation). It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses (whole-brain contrasts with coordinates and thresholding) and multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., incompatible vs. neutral, effect tones vs. neutral). Participants are healthy adults; results are reported as coordinates, figures, and tables. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Thus all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation of covert auditory spatial attention/orienting in congenitally blind and sighted individuals. While it reports whole-brain, voxelwise within-group task contrasts (e.g., cues>baseline, targets>baseline) and includes appropriate group-level analyses, the experimental task probes spatial attention/orienting rather than an executive function domain specified by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (any participant group allowed), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task assessing executive function/cognitive control), I6 (task within listed executive function domains). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study of intrinsic alertness (vigilance), which falls within the executive domains listed (I6). The study reports group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM (subtraction of alertness vs control/fixation) and provides coordinates/tables and figures of whole-brain results (Table 1, path analysis based on voxelwise activations), satisfying within-group contrasts (alertness vs fixation). Although the paper emphasizes subsequent connectivity (CSEM), activation maps and voxelwise group contrasts are reported and used to define network nodes, so it does not meet exclusion E4. Partial slice coverage is acceptable per I7 and the study performed voxelwise group analyses. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study includes a classic executive-function task (Stroop; inhibition domain) and a task-based moral-dilemma paradigm. Group-level, voxelwise analyses are reported (ICA-derived spatial maps, voxelwise paired-samples t tests, and tables of coordinates/cluster statistics are provided), and within-group task contrasts (task vs rest/fixation and task-condition contrasts) are described. Whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in tables and supplemental materials. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI (within-group contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise maps, coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function/cognitive control (time-estimation feedback and Stroop tasks). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (contrasts such as incongruent>congruent and errors>correct in the Stroop task; feedback contrasts in the time-estimation task) with figures/tables, and at least one within-group task contrast. Participant group is healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Although slice coverage was limited to 28 slices, analyses were voxelwise (partial-brain acquisition still qualifies). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

Excluded due to E3: the report uses ROI-based analyses (mean time series within anatomically defined Brodmann ROIs) and presents region-level statistics; I find no evidence of a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain statistical map or coordinate tables/figures that would qualify as voxelwise results. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI on an executive control task — POP), I6 (task falls within executive domains: attentional control/motor planning/inhibition), I8 (within-group contrasts of low vs. high load reported), I9 (participant groups reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no voxelwise group-level maps reported), I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded under E3.

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study that examines action selection/preparation and working memory processes modulated by reward expectation — fitting executive function domains (planning, working memory, vigilance). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM99 (main effects and within-group contrasts: specific vs non-specific preparation; reward vs no-reward; interaction), with coordinates/tables and figures. Participants were healthy volunteers (within-group contrasts are reported). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports task-based fMRI (and lesion behavioural data) that directly examines initiation/programming of repetitive movements — initiation is listed among eligible executive domains. The study reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (single taps and repetitive taps vs rest), with whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and tabulated Talairach coordinates. Although slice coverage did not extend to the entire brain (partial-brain acquisition), I7 explicitly allows partial coverage provided voxelwise analyses were performed. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E6 violations). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (voxelwise, group-level fMRI analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (within-group sample reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/tables). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 and I6 — the study investigates visuospatial attention and implicit visuomotor responses to graspable objects rather than an established executive function/cognitive control domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the task uses cueing and a go/no-go design, the primary contrasts and authors' focus are on attentional orienting and visuomotor processing rather than executive control processes targeted by the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), so exclusion is due to not meeting I5/I6 rather than missing information.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a modified emotional Stroop paradigm that probes cognitive control/inhibition over emotional interference (an executive function). The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (emotional incongruence vs congruence) with voxelwise one-sample t-tests and cluster thresholds, and provides regional results (Table 1, figures) for both healthy controls and patients with schizophrenia. Thus it supplies whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps (voxelwise analyses) and within-group contrasts for participant groups, meeting all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI, task-based study using a continuous performance task (CPT) probing vigilance/attentional modulation of motor function (an executive domain). The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain SPM2 analyses (task vs baseline and degraded vs non-degraded contrasts) with coordinate tables and psycho-physiological interaction analyses. At least one within-group task contrast is reported for participant groups. Partial slice coverage was used but analyses were voxelwise and whole-brain/ROI-masked as described, which satisfies the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group activations). Full text is present (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly manipulates and measures executive-control-relevant processes (lexical selection and Go/No-Go response initiation/inhibition). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM analyses (e.g., Selection vs No-Selection; Go vs No-Go; active tasks vs fixation) with voxelwise and cluster-corrected thresholds, and provides coordinates/tables and figures of whole-brain activations. Although one run used partial coverage focused on SMA, analyses were voxelwise and group-level (partial-brain acquisition is allowed by criteria). Full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a spatial Stroop conflict paradigm that probes executive control/inhibition. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (e.g., informative position vs. neutral cue contrasts, P–N; W–N; P–W) and voxelwise regression analyses relating preparatory activity to behavioral cueing effects. These are within-group task contrasts analyzed with random-effects group statistics. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and therefore appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Given these points, the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates proactive response inhibition and executive control induced by cueing methods. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., mixed-block no-cue vs. pure-block no-cue) with stereotaxic coordinates (Table 1) and interprets activations in inhibition/monitoring regions (superior parietal lobule, precuneus, posterior cingulate, thalamus). The paradigm and contrasts probe inhibition/executive-control processes (an established EF domain) and include within-group task contrasts. The imaging analysis used random-effects, voxelwise group maps suitable for meta-analysis. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Included for meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a Stroop task (inhibition/cognitive control), meeting the executive-function domain requirement. The paper reports voxelwise group-level GLM analyses and whole-brain statistical maps (group average z-maps) with coordinates/tables and figures. Within-group task contrasts are presented (e.g., incongruent vs. neutral Stroop; Stroop vs. null), and results are reported for a healthy adult sample. All relevant core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of the antisaccade task, which probes inhibitory control (an executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., correct antisaccades vs prosaccades; correct vs error antisaccades) with stereotaxic coordinates and cluster thresholds, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise evidence despite partial slice coverage. Within-group task contrasts are explicitly reported. Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable. Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study reporting group-level voxelwise activation maps for task contrasts (block localizers and event-related gap and memory-delay contrasts). The memory-delay paradigm involves holding spatial information over a delay (working memory) and the gap paradigm probes preparatory/ initiation processes; both fall within executive-function domains (working memory, initiation/planning). Whole-brain voxelwise analyses and corrected statistical maps are reported; partial-slice coverage is allowed per criteria and voxelwise analyses were used. Within-group task contrasts (saccade/pointing vs fixation; memory-delay/gap durations) are presented. Participant group is healthy adults and results are reported as voxelwise maps and timecourses. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study with healthy participants that reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., V+ vs ND, V+ vs V−, V+ vs invalid) using random-effects SPM analyses and reports coordinates/figures. The task is a target-detection/Posner cueing paradigm requiring sustained monitoring and anticipatory allocation of attention (interpretable under the ‘vigilance’/attentional control domain within the inclusion list). Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented and within-group contrasts are explicitly reported. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, empirical data present). Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is eligible for inclusion.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrast Attend vs Regulate reported), I9 (healthy adult participant group reported), I10 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I6 — the experimental paradigm targets cognitive emotion regulation of conditioned fear (emotion regulation/extinction), which does not clearly fall within the specified executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the study invokes cognitive control and engages dlPFC, the primary task and theoretical focus are on emotion regulation/ fear extinction rather than a canonical executive function domain required by the review. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered.

The study is an event-related fMRI experiment with group-level voxelwise analyses and within-group contrasts, but the task is a Posner spatial orienting (endogenous/exogenous attention) paradigm rather than an executive function task as defined by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task-based Go/No-go response inhibition paradigm (Error Awareness Task) assessing executive control (inhibition). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (scanning parameters, preprocessing, voxelwise group analyses), Results (group-level t-maps, cluster thresholds, coordinates), and Discussion. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (one-sample t tests, cluster-corrected) and provides coordinates (Table 1), and performs within-group contrasts (Aware vs Unaware errors; events vs baseline). Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study explicitly investigating cognitive control/conflict monitoring during recognition (rejecting novel objects in familiar contexts). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise NO>NN contrasts and reports peak coordinates and cluster results. The NO versus NN contrast is a within-group task contrast (examined within young and elderly and used to relate activation to performance), and group-level random-effects analyses are reported. Participants include healthy young and elderly adults. Reporting includes tables/coordinates and full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (satisfying I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10), the task (visual–spatial orienting; exogenous/endogenous facilitation and inhibition of return) probes attentional orienting mechanisms rather than an executive function domain as defined by the review (working memory, inhibition in the cognitive-control sense such as response inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The study’s IOR is an attentional phenomenon and not a canonical executive inhibition task (e.g., Go/No-go, Stroop). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDED because I6 not met; inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10; inclusion criteria not met: I6.

This is an fMRI task-based study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (random-effects second-level analyses) and tables/figures of activation. The number bisection task includes clear components of executive control (monitoring, inhibition, cognitive set changes, working-memory demands) and the authors specifically report contrasts isolating cognitive-set change (bisection possibility; right VLPFC) and monitoring/inhibition (superior frontal gyrus/angular gyrus). Within-group task contrasts (parametric regressors for bisected and non-bisected triplets) are presented. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets I5 (fMRI task assessing cognitive control), I6 (task involves executive domains: monitoring/inhibition/set-shifting/working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (within-group healthy adult sample), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is excluded because it does not assess an executive function or cognitive-control task per the meta-analysis definition. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none (no exclusion criteria triggered). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts such as anger vs. neutral), I9 (participant group qualified: healthy adults with within-group contrasts), I10 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I5 (study does not assess executive function/cognitive control; it examines emotional prosody and attention in social cognition), I6 (tasks do not fall within specified executive domains — primary task was a gender-decision and emotion/attention manipulation, not working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Full text appears complete and was reviewed. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I5 and I6 are not satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study examining cognitive control/executive function (representation and maintenance of context, selection) during a missing-letter language production task. Inclusion criteria: I5 satisfied—uses fMRI and assesses cognitive control; I6 satisfied—task engages working memory/maintenance and selection (working memory domain of executive function); I7 satisfied—reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects GLM, AFNI; reported whole-brain activation maps/coordinates); I8 satisfied—reports within-group task contrasts (context vs neutral; context-appropriate vs context-inappropriate; selection demand contrasts); I9 satisfied—within-group contrasts on healthy adult participants; I10 satisfied—whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation using task-based Stroop paradigms that probe inhibitory/cognitive control processes (executive function). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (incongruent-minus-neutral and negative-minus-neutral) and group-level paired t-test maps derived from whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded and cluster-corrected). Thus it provides task-evoked, within-group, voxelwise results suitable for pooling. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study directly investigates cognitive control/conflict monitoring (ACC, DLPFC) during a task-based moral judgment paradigm that requires inhibiting prepotent emotional responses (i.e., cognitive control/inhibition). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (and ROI-restricted analyses), and within-group contrasts (high-RT vs low-RT personal trials; utilitarian vs nonutilitarian trials) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster corrections. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, analysis), Results, and Discussion, so core article content is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses of task contrasts relevant to cognitive control/conflict processing. The experiment required synesthetes to perform a speeded response (button press) indicating synesthetic experience and includes within-group contrasts (e.g., C− S+ > C− S−; interaction contrasts) that reveal activation in DLPFC associated with perceptual conflict and supervisory cognitive control. Whole-brain fixed- and random-effects SPM analyses are reported with stereotactic coordinates in tables and figures. Participants are a defined group (grapheme-color synesthetes), which is acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function/task activations that pools across participant groups.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that probes attentional/cognitive-control processes (challenge-driven attention), operationalized via an audiovisual simultaneity detection task that requires sustained/vigilant allocation of resources under unpredictability. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, second-level random-effects analyses (difficulty-weighted contrasts and task vs null), with whole-brain voxelwise maps (despite partial slice coverage: 21 axial slices). Results are reported in text and figures and include MNI coordinates and ROI analyses. Participants were a within-group sample of healthy adults (n=12). Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for an fMRI task assessing executive/cognitive-control-related vigilance, provides voxelwise group-level activation maps, includes within-group contrasts, and reports whole-brain results in the manuscript.

This is an fMRI task study with within-group contrasts of selection (select 10/30 > 70/90) in adolescents and adults and targets cognitive-control regions. However, the main analyses were restricted to a priori anatomical ROIs with small-volume correction (3 mm spheres) and voxelwise tests only within those ROIs. The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map; results are ROI/SVC-based. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI/SVC-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task probes cognitive control/conflict monitoring), I8 (within-group contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group map).

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation contrasts (random-effects SPM analyses) comparing task conditions. The paradigm manipulates intentional/top-down control (instructions to ‘remember’ vs ‘look’), which falls under the executive domain of initiation/top-down cognitive control, and yields within-group task contrasts (e.g., high-intention encoding vs low-intention encoding; high-intention recognition vs low-intention re-viewing). Whole-brain results are reported (FDR-corrected maps and coordinates), and participant groups are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study that directly investigates cognitive control/executive processes (strategic ordering, selection, working memory, monitoring) during temporal context retrieval and non-memory ordering tasks, using task-based paradigms. The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM2 analyses (with coordinates/tables and ROI follow-ups) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., recency > ordering; stimulus number and response number manipulations). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise activations and coordinate tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

execution_stats.search_query: (((("functional magnetic resonance imaging"[Mesh] OR fMRI[tiab] OR "magnetic resonance imaging"[tiab] OR "positron emission tomography"[Mesh] OR PET[tiab])) AND (("executive function"[Mesh] OR "executive function*"[tiab] OR "cognitive control"[tiab] OR "working memory"[Mesh] OR "working memory"[tiab] OR inhibition[tiab] OR inhibitory[tiab] OR "cognitive flexibility"[tiab] OR "set shifting"[tiab] OR "task switching"[tiab] OR planning[tiab] OR vigilance[tiab] OR "sustained attention"[tiab] OR initiation[tiab] OR "go/no-go"[tiab] OR "go no go"[tiab] OR "stop signal"[tiab] OR stroop[tiab] OR "n-back"[tiab] OR "tower of london"[tiab] OR "tower of hanoi"[tiab] OR "wisconsin card sorting"[tiab] OR "continuous performance task"[tiab]))) AND Humans[mh] AND English[lang]) NOT (review[pt] OR "systematic review"[tiab] OR meta-analysis[pt]))
